Name: Loaded Return Shipment
Documentation: **A loaded return shipment** carries returned items, a Return Authorization reference, destination, and handling instructions. It is issued when all returned items are loaded and secured, and its arrival indicates the return conveyance is ready to depart. With it, departure occurs and transit to the return destination begins. This handover protects against the return conveyance waiting at the loading point and the Return Authorization remaining open.

Name: Packed Return
Documentation: **A packed return shipment** contains returned items and a packing list referencing the Return Authorization. It is issued when returned items are packed into shipping units and labelled for return, and its arrival means the return is ready to load. With it, loading begins and the return moves toward transport. This handover protects against loading having no return shipment to place on transport and the return remaining staged.

Name: Picked Return
Documentation: **Returned items picked from storage** carry item identifiers, quantities, and a Return Authorization reference. They are issued when returned items are retrieved and verified against the Return Authorization, and their arrival means the return items are ready for packing. With them, packing of return items starts and each item receives return packaging. This handover protects against packing having no return items to process and the Return Authorization waiting unfulfilled.

Name: Return Authorization
Documentation: **Return authorization allows inspection** A Return Authorization permits a return, specifying items, quantities, reason, disposition instructions, and validity. It is issued only after a return request is evaluated and approved, so its arrival tells inspection that the return is authorized. Inspection and examination of returned items proceed against the authorized list, with every returned item examined and a disposition decision made. This prevents returned items from sitting unexamined and disposition from going undecided.

Name: Return Authorization
Documentation: **Return authorization opens receiving** A Return Authorization permits a return, specifying items, quantities, reason, disposition instructions, and validity. It is issued only after a return request is evaluated and approved, so its arrival tells receiving that the return is authorized. Receiving of returned items proceeds and items are accepted into return handling, ensuring returned goods do not remain with the returning party. The authorized item list guides receiving staff in verifying what is returned.

Name: Return Authorization
Documentation: **Return authorization starts inspection** A Return Authorization permits a return, specifying items, quantities, reason, disposition instructions, and validity. It is issued only after a return request is evaluated and approved, so its arrival tells inspection that the return is authorized. Inspection of returned items starts with authorization in hand, proceeding to examine each item and produce a disposition decision. This prevents returned items from sitting uninspected and ensures a disposition decision is made for each.

Name: Return Authorization
Documentation: **Return authorization permits receiving** A Return Authorization grants permission for a return, listing items, quantities, reason, disposition instructions, and validity. It is issued only after a return request is evaluated and approved, so receiving knows the return is authorized. Receiving of returned items proceeds and items are accepted into return handling, so returned goods never remain with the returning party. The authorized item list supports verification and acceptance. This handover ensures the return handling process begins without delay.

Name: Return Authorization
Documentation: **Return authorization clears unloading** A Return Authorization permits a return, specifying items, quantities, reason, disposition instructions, and validity. It is issued only after a return request is evaluated and approved, so its arrival authorizes unloading of returned items. Unloading proceeds and items are removed from transport, ensuring returned goods do not remain on the vehicle. The authorization serves as the go-ahead for dock workers to offload the return, preventing transport from being held up.

Name: Return Shipment Schedule
Documentation: **Return shipment schedule drives loading** A schedule that assigns return shipments to transport, with pickup times, loading slots, and destination. Issued when return transportation is scheduled and confirmed, its arrival provides the return shipment with a loading slot. The loading slot is used and the return shipment is loaded on time, preventing delays from unscheduled loading. With this schedule in hand, the return shipment moves efficiently through the loading process without waiting.

Name: Return Shipment Schedule
Documentation: **Return shipment schedule sets pickup times** loading slots, and destination for each return. It is issued when return transportation is scheduled and confirmed; its arrival provides the return shipment with a pickup time. Packing sequence aligns to that pickup time so the return is ready when transport arrives. This handover means packing finishes with a transport commitment already in place, and staged returns are never left without a scheduled pickup.

Name: Return Shipment Schedule
Documentation: **Return shipment schedule sets pickup times** loading slots, and destination for each return. It is issued when return transportation is scheduled and confirmed, and its arrival provides the return shipment with a pickup time. Picking then aligns its sequence to that pickup time, which becomes the deadline for retrieving return items. This handover gives picking a clear deadline and ensures return items are ready when transport arrives, rather than leaving the return unprepared.

Name: Return Shipment Schedule
Documentation: **Return shipment schedule sets pickup times** loading slots, and destination for each return. Issued when return transportation is scheduled and confirmed, its arrival provides the return shipment with a departure time. Shipping then departs at that scheduled time, so the return conveyance leaves as planned. This handover gives shipping a definite departure time, ensuring departure occurs at the scheduled time and the return conveyance is never left idle waiting for that departure.

Name: Invoice
Documentation: **An invoice for delivered goods** carries amount, payment terms, line items, and references to Customer Order and Shipment. It is issued after shipment or service delivery is confirmed, and its arrival means payment approval starts. With it, payment approval reviews the invoice against contract and delivery proof, and the approved invoice proceeds to payment. This handover protects against payment approval having no invoice to review and payment not being requested.

Name: Loaded Shipment
Documentation: **A shipment loaded onto outbound transport** carries items, destination, and delivery instructions. It is issued when all items for a customer order are loaded and secured, and its arrival means the shipment is ready to depart. With it, departure occurs and delivery transit begins. This handover protects against the shipment remaining at the dock and the Customer Order not being fulfilled.

Name: Packed Shipment
Documentation: **Packed Shipment triggers loading.** When all items for a customer order are packed and labelled, this sealed shipment, containing the ordered items and a packing list, is issued. Its arrival means the shipment is ready for loading. Loading then places the shipment onto transport. This handover ensures that loading has a shipment to process, so the order moves out of the packing area and is placed on transport, rather than remaining stationary.

Name: Packed Shipment
Documentation: **Packed Shipment enables transport scheduling.** When the packing completes, this sealed shipment, containing ordered items, weight, dimensions, and destination, is issued. Its arrival provides all the shipment details needed to arrange transport. Transport scheduling then uses the packed shipment's weight, dimensions, and destination to assign a carrier. This handover gives transport scheduling the shipment specifics it needs, so a pickup is arranged immediately without delay and no shipment remains unassigned.

Name: Picked Items
Documentation: **Items picked from inventory** for a customer order carry item identifiers, quantities, and location. They are issued when items are retrieved from storage and confirmed against the Fulfilment Order, and their arrival means the items are ready for packing. With them, packing begins and each item is placed into shipment packaging. This handover protects against packing having no items to pack and the Fulfilment Order remaining incomplete.

Name: Inquiry Response
Documentation: **Customer inquiry response** puts the answer, resolution status, and references to the customer order or account into the hands of the team that will close the case. It is produced once research is complete and a clear response is prepared, and its arrival signals that the inquiry is ready to close. Receiving it lets the inquiry be formally closed with the response recorded, so the customer gets a definitive answer and the case does not remain open or unresolved.

Name: Inventory Record
Documentation: **Inventory record for received items** captures quantities, locations, and status after goods are staged and recorded in the system. This handover activates picking: once it arrives, the items are visible in inventory and become available for pickers to select from the recorded locations. That visibility lets picking fill open orders directly from the stated spots, so received stock never sits undiscovered and orders are not held up because items are missing from the pick list.

Name: Shipment Plan
Documentation: **Customer shipment plan** carries the destination, delivery window, and consolidation requirements for a shipment, produced when order routing finalizes the shipment's path and the required delivery date. Its arrival signals that transportation now has a shipment plan to schedule. With this plan, scheduling assigns a carrier and confirms a pickup time, turning the shipment into a committed transport movement. The plan's arrival prevents the shipment from sitting without a carrier assignment or a confirmed pickup, keeping the delivery on track.

Name: Transportation Schedule
Documentation: **Transportation Schedule enables loading.** When a carrier is confirmed and a pickup time is set, this schedule for outbound shipment pickup, including carrier, time, and dock assignment, is issued. Its arrival means the shipment has a loading slot. Loading then proceeds at the assigned dock and time. This handover gives loading the carrier and time it requires, so the shipment moves into the loading process without waiting for a carrier or a time.

Name: Shipment
Documentation: **Shipment enables invoicing.** When the shipment departs, this record confirms that goods have left the facility, with ship date, tracking reference, and delivered items. Its arrival means delivery has occurred, giving invoicing a verifiable record that the goods were actually shipped. Invoicing then generates the invoice using these shipment details. This handover provides the proof of shipment invoicing requires, so the customer order is billed promptly and no order remains unbilled.

Name: Fulfilment Order
Documentation: **A Fulfilment Order authorises packing.** Issued after order validation passes and inventory is allocated, it carries the items, quantities, packaging requirements, and customer address. Its arrival signals that the order is ready for packing. Packing then proceeds according to this instruction, applying the required packaging and preparing the order for shipment. This handover is what prevents packing from lacking the instruction it needs, which would leave the order unprepared for shipment.

Name: Fulfilment Order
Documentation: **A Fulfilment Order directs picking.** After order validation passes and inventory is allocated, the Fulfilment Order is issued with the precise items, quantities, and storage locations needed for retrieval. Its arrival signals that the order is ready for picking. Picking then proceeds to retrieve the specified items from the correct storage locations. This handover protects against picking having no list of items to retrieve, which would otherwise leave inventory completely untouched.

Name: Fulfilment Order
Documentation: **A Fulfilment Order triggers routing.** Issued after order validation passes and inventory is allocated, it carries the items, quantities, delivery address, and requested delivery date. Its arrival signals that the order is ready for routing and scheduling. Routing then determines the shipment path and delivery requirements. This handover provides routing with the order details needed to plan the shipment, preventing planning from stalling for lack of an order to route.

Name: Customer Order
Documentation: **Customer Order initiates inquiry with context.** Issued when a customer places an order, the Customer Order specifies the requested items, quantities, delivery address, and terms. Its arrival begins an inquiry about the order with those order details available, giving the inquiry the exact order context it needs. This ensures the inquiry has the context required for resolution and is not left unresolved.

Name: Customer Order
Documentation: **Customer Order grounds return authorization.** Issued when a customer places an order, the Customer Order specifies requested items, quantities, delivery address, and terms. Its arrival logs a return request against the original order, giving the return request its basis and providing the authorization evaluation with a concrete order to reference. This ensures return authorization evaluation proceeds with the original order in view, giving it the foundation needed to make a decision.

Name: Customer Order
Documentation: **Customer Order drives invoice preparation.** Issued when a customer places an order, the Customer Order specifies requested items, quantities, delivery address, and terms. Its arrival means invoicing uses the order lines and pricing to prepare an invoice. The order lines and pricing carried by the order are the only basis for the invoice. This handover supplies the authoritative order data invoicing needs, ensuring an invoice is prepared and a bill is issued rather than no bill at all.

Name: Customer Order
Documentation: **Customer Order directs packing decisions.** Issued when a customer places an order, the Customer Order specifies requested items, quantities, delivery address, and terms. Its arrival means packing uses the customer order to determine what to pack. The order lines and quantities carried by the order are the exact packing list. This handover gives packing the authoritative order data needed to assemble the shipment, ensuring a shipment is prepared rather than no shipment at all.

Name: Customer Order
Documentation: **When a customer places an order**, the **Customer Order** carries the requested items, quantities, delivery address, and terms for that purchase. Inquiry processing relies on this order to find status and details; it uses the order as the authoritative reference for any customer question. The handover ensures inquiry processing always has accurate order information, so responses are correct. This handover protects inquiry processing from responding incorrectly by supplying the order information it needs.

Name: Customer Order
Documentation: **When a customer places an order**, the **Customer Order** carries the requested items, quantities, delivery address, and terms for that purchase. Inventory reservation uses this order to hold the ordered items against that specific customer order, in the quantities requested. This handover makes the inventory unavailable to other orders, protecting the customer's allocation. By supplying the order, inventory reservation reserves the items and prevents them from remaining available for other orders.

Name: Customer Order
Documentation: **When a customer places an order**, the **Customer Order** carries the requested items, quantities, delivery address, and terms for that purchase. Transportation scheduling receives the delivery address and requested date from this order, so the transport planner knows where and when the order must arrive. This handover allows scheduling to arrange the necessary transport for the order. By providing these details, the order ensures a transport schedule is created, so the order has transport arranged.

Name: Customer Order
Documentation: **When a customer places an order**, the **Customer Order** carries the requested items, quantities, delivery address, and terms for that purchase. Shipping uses this order to verify the outbound shipment, checking that the right items and quantities are packed and sent. This handover ensures the shipment has a specific order to fulfil. By providing the order, shipping confirms the outbound shipment matches what the customer requested, protecting against shipping errors.

Name: Customer Order
Documentation: **When a customer places an order**, the **Customer Order** carries the requested items, quantities, delivery address, and terms for that purchase. Invoicing uses the order lines and pricing from this order to prepare the customer's bill, including quantities and any applicable terms. This handover gives invoicing the exact items, prices, and terms to include on the invoice. By supplying the order, invoicing generates an invoice, ensuring a bill is issued for the purchase.

Name: Customer Order
Documentation: **When a customer places an order**, the **Customer Order** carries the requested items, quantities, delivery address, and terms for that purchase. Validation checks the order's completeness and transforms it into a Fulfilment Order as the source for downstream work. This handover starts the fulfilment process by giving validation a complete order to process, protecting against stalled fulfilment. By providing the order, validation checks completeness and creates the Fulfilment Order, ensuring fulfilment begins.

Name: Customer Order
Documentation: **When a customer places an order**, the **Customer Order** carries the requested items, quantities, delivery address, and terms for that purchase. Engineering receives the specific order requirements from this order and completes all necessary custom specifications for the ordered item. This handover gives engineering the precise, detailed requirements needed to fully engineer the order. By providing the order, engineering completes the custom specifications, ensuring the order does not remain unengineered.

Name: Customer Order
Documentation: **When a customer places an order**, the **Customer Order** carries the requested items, quantities, delivery address, and terms for that purchase. This order allows a project order to be created for complex fulfilment, with a work breakdown and execution plan. The handover gives the project the structure needed to manage the work. By providing the customer order, a project order is created, so the fulfilment has a project work breakdown and execution plan.

Name: Customer Order
Documentation: **A Customer Order carries** the requested items, quantities, delivery address, and terms. When a customer places an order, this Customer Order is issued to update or re-enter the order with additional information. Its arrival signals that the order record has been refreshed with the details needed for the next step. That refresh is what prevents the order from remaining incomplete. The handover ensures downstream processing starts with a complete order instead of being blocked by an incomplete one.

Name: Customer Order
Documentation: **A Customer Order carries** the requested items, quantities, delivery address, and terms that define the order needs. When a customer places an order, this Customer Order establishes the demand signal that sourcing acts on. Its arrival means the order's needs are gathered as sourcing demand. That handover gives sourcing the specific demand signal required to plan inputs, protecting against a situation where sourcing has no demand signal and no inputs are planned.

Name: Customer Order
Documentation: **A Customer Order carries** requested items, quantities, delivery address, and terms. When a customer places an order, this Customer Order provides the delivery instructions that delivery planning acts on. Its arrival means delivery demand is gathered from those instructions, converting the delivery address and terms into a concrete demand signal. That handover gives delivery planning the demand it needs to allocate transport capacity, protecting against delivery planning having no demand and no allocated transport capacity.

Name: Customer Order
Documentation: **A Customer Order records** a committed purchase, carrying line items with quantities, requested delivery dates, pricing, delivery location, and a unique order reference. It is issued once the customer accepts the offer and the order passes validation against price and availability rules. On arrival, demand aggregation consumes the order lines to update the demand signal and drive supply planning. This handover ensures the committed requirement is part of the demand picture, so supply planning includes this volume and the order is not left unfulfilled.

Name: Invoice
Documentation: **Invoice for delivered order or service** details the amount due, payment terms, invoice number, line items, quantities, and the reference to the fulfilled order or shipment. It is issued only after the related shipment or service has been delivered and billing terms are met. Once it arrives, payment approval reviews the invoice against the purchase order or contract and schedules payment, clearing the path for on-time supplier payment and ensuring the supplier balance does not remain open for lack of an invoice.

Name: Load Confirmation
Documentation: **Load confirmation for completed vehicle** records the vehicle identifier, loaded piece counts, weights, and the sequence of stops. It is issued only after every shipment assigned to that vehicle has been placed, secured, and matched to the shipping schedule by weight. When it arrives, the outbound shipment is released to the carrier and the load is cleared to depart, so the vehicle does not sit at the dock and outgoing shipments move on schedule. This confirmation is the last step before the load leaves.

Name: Packed Shipment
Documentation: **Packed Shipment carries dispatch-ready sealed units** prepared for dispatch, with package identifiers, weights, dimensions, and the associated order reference. It is issued when packing completes, every item passes pack verification, and the packing slip is attached. Load planning then assigns the total packaged sets to a vehicle bay and a route position. This handover gives the dock a completed unit to load, ensuring the shipment moves out of packing instead of remaining there.

Name: Packed Shipment
Documentation: **Packed Shipment carries dispatch-ready sealed units** prepared for dispatch, with package identifiers, weights, dimensions, and the associated order reference. It is issued when packing completes, every item passes pack verification, and the packing slip is attached. Transportation scheduling then uses the dimensions, weight, and destination to select a carrier and confirm a pickup window. This handover ensures a carrier is booked and packaged goods are not left waiting in packing.

Name: Packing Slip
Documentation: **Packing Slip lists package contents** including item numbers, quantities, and any special handling instructions for each package. It is generated at the completion of packing and travels with the physical package to the carrier handover. Shipment verification at handover to the carrier uses this list to confirm counts and conditions. This handover gives the carrier a manifest of contents, so shipment counts and conditions are confirmed, and disputes are resolved later.

Name: Packing Slip
Documentation: **Packing Slip lists package contents** including item numbers, quantities, and any special handling instructions for each package. It is generated at the completion of packing and travels with the physical package. Loading uses it at the dock to reconcile cartons against the load plan before any carton is placed on a vehicle. This handover gives the loader an item-level check, so misloads are caught before departure and do not go undetected.

Name: Packed Shipment
Documentation: **A completed Packed Shipment** carries sealed cartons or pallets with package identifiers, weights, dimensions, and the order reference. It is handed over only when packing is complete, every item passes verification, and the packing slip is attached. This means load planning immediately assigns the packaged sets to a vehicle bay and a route position. The dock receives a finished unit ready to load, so the shipment does not remain stuck in packing.

Name: Picked Items
Documentation: **Picked items are physical goods** retrieved from inventory, carrying SKU, quantity, lot or serial number, and the order reference. They are produced when the picker confirms each line on the pick list and collects the correct quantity. Packing then receives these goods and matches them to the order lines, starting the packing process. This handover gives packing the physical units required for its work, preventing an order from remaining unpacked due to a lack of items.

Name: Picked Items
Documentation: **Picked items are physical goods** retrieved from inventory, carrying SKU, quantity, lot or serial number, and the order reference. They are produced when the picker confirms each line on the pick list and collects the correct quantity. Packing then receives these goods and matches them to the order lines, starting the packing process. This handover gives packing the physical units required for its work, preventing an order from remaining unpacked due to a lack of items.

Name: Inquiry Response
Documentation: **Inquiry response for resolution** carries the answer to the customer question, the resolution status, and the original inquiry reference. It is issued once the inquiry has been investigated and a definitive response is ready for the customer. When this response arrives, the inquiry is marked resolved and the customer is notified of the outcome, closing the case so it does not remain open and ensuring the customer always gets an answer. That closes the loop and leaves the customer with a clear resolution.

Name: Pick List
Documentation: **A Pick List specifies the items** to be collected for one or more orders, including locations, quantities, and the order line reference. It is issued once inventory has been reserved and the picking wave is released. The picker uses this document to retrieve the listed items from the designated storage locations. This handover ensures the picker knows exactly what to collect and where, which keeps the order moving forward instead of stalling for lack of direction.

Name: Pick List
Documentation: **A Pick List specifies the items** to be collected for one or more orders, including locations, quantities, and the order line reference. It is issued once inventory has been reserved and the picking wave is released. The picker uses this document to retrieve the listed items from the designated storage locations. This handover ensures the picker knows exactly what to collect and where, which keeps the order moving forward instead of stalling for lack of direction.

Name: Shipping Schedule
Documentation: **A Shipping Schedule assigns dock doors**, loading windows, carrier details, and the sequence of vehicle loading for a set of shipments. It is issued once transportation is arranged and carrier pickup times are confirmed. Loading operations then stage the packaged shipments at the assigned door in the scheduled order. This handover gives the loading team a defined timing and location plan, preventing loading from happening ad hoc or not at all.

Name: Shipment Notification
Documentation: **Shipment Notification carries** the carrier reference, tracking number, expected delivery date, and the list of shipped order lines. It is issued the moment the carrier accepts the shipment and the goods leave the organization’s control. Billing uses that notification to confirm shipment and generate the invoice, and because it carries the dispatch details, invoicing proceeds without delay. That proof of dispatch is what prevents the billing process from stalling while waiting for confirmation.

Name: Shipment Notification
Documentation: **Shipment Notification carries** the carrier reference, tracking number, expected delivery date, and the list of shipped order lines. It is issued the moment the carrier accepts the shipment and the goods leave the organization’s control. Inquiry handling uses that notification to give the customer tracking status and an expected delivery date. That current shipment detail is what allows customer inquiries to be resolved accurately, instead of leaving them unanswered for lack of dispatch information.

Name: Proof of Delivery
Documentation: **Proof of Delivery records** the recipient’s signature, the delivery date and time, and any noted shortages or damages. It is obtained when the shipment is handed to the customer or their agent at the delivery location. Settlement confirmation uses that signed proof to verify fulfilment and release payment, because the signed record is evidence that delivery actually occurred. That evidence is what prevents payment from being held for lack of proof.

Name: Proof of Delivery
Documentation: **Proof of Delivery records** the recipient’s signature, the delivery date and time, and any noted shortages or damages. It is obtained when the shipment is handed to the customer or their agent at the delivery location. Billing attaches that proof to the invoice as evidence that the delivery was completed. That attached evidence is what allows collection to proceed immediately, because the invoice now carries the proof that delivery actually happened, so there is no reason for delay.

Name: Shipment Notification
Documentation: **Shipment Notification gives receiving advance notice** A Shipment Notification carries the carrier reference, tracking number, expected delivery date, and the list of shipped order lines. It is issued when the carrier accepts the shipment and the goods leave the organization's control. On arrival, this notice lets receiving prepare dock space and staff for the inbound delivery, ensuring the delivery does not arrive unannounced and receiving is not left unprepared for the shipment.

Name: Shipment Notification
Documentation: **Shipment Notification allows receiving readiness** This notice carries the carrier reference, tracking number, expected delivery date, and the list of shipped order lines. It is issued when the carrier accepts the shipment and the goods leave the organization's control. With this advance information, receiving can prepare dock space and staff in time for the inbound delivery, which means the delivery does not arrive unannounced and the dock is not left unprepared.

Name: Shipment Notification
Documentation: **Shipment Notification lets unloading plan ahead** This notice carries the carrier reference, tracking number, expected delivery date, and the list of shipped order lines. It is issued when the carrier accepts the shipment and the goods leave the organization's control. With this information, unloading can plan the sequence and resources for the incoming vehicle, so the dock knows exactly which vehicle to expect and unloading does not have to be reactive.

Name: Change Portfolio Analysis
Documentation: **Change Portfolio Assessment guides action.** The Change Portfolio Assessment records the current set of proposed changes with scores for strategic fit, cost exposure, risk level, and implementation readiness, plus explicit dependencies and a recommended priority order. It is issued only after every pending change has been assessed against the current portfolio budget and strategic objectives. Its arrival completes the assessment and makes the ranked change set available. Action planning begins with the ranked changes and their dependencies, so sequencing and resource allocation follow the assessed priorities and portfolio impact.

Name: Change Portfolio Analysis
Documentation: **Change Portfolio Assessment informs budgets.** The Change Portfolio Assessment records the current set of proposed changes with scores for strategic fit, cost exposure, risk level, and implementation readiness, plus explicit dependencies and a recommended priority order. It is issued only after every pending change has been assessed against the current portfolio budget and strategic objectives. Its arrival completes the assessment and makes the ranked change set available. Budget change proposals draw on the recorded cost and benefit estimates, so funding adjustments align with the priority order and resource conflicts remain visible.

Name: Training Portfolio Analysis
Documentation: **Training portfolio evaluation informs action planning.** The Training Portfolio Assessment records current training programmes, participation levels, completion rates, and alignment to competency requirements. It is issued after all offerings have been evaluated against workforce capability needs, marking an evaluated portfolio ready for action. Action planning uses the assessment to select training initiatives, assign ownership, and focus resources on programmes that close specific capability gaps. This handover gives planning a clear view of which programmes close which gaps, so initiative selection is based on real gap coverage.

Name: Training Portfolio Analysis
Documentation: **Evaluated training portfolio guides competency planning.** The Training Portfolio Assessment records current training programmes, participation levels, completion rates, and alignment to competency requirements. It is issued after all offerings have been evaluated against workforce capability needs, marking an evaluated portfolio ready for action. Competency development planning draws on the assessment to target specific skill areas and sequence learning interventions. The handover supplies evaluated training effectiveness and current participation, ensuring the plan builds on evidence of what already works.

Name: Budget Gap Assessment
Documentation: **Quantified budget gaps inform action planning.** The Budget Gap Assessment identifies differences between budgeted and required funding for approved initiatives, with gap amounts and drivers. It is issued after budget data has been compared against baseline and proposed commitments, meaning gaps are quantified and attributed. Action planning incorporates these quantified funding gaps and their drivers into initiative decisions. The assessment ensures that planning knows which initiatives face shortfalls and why, allowing decisions to address real funding pressures.

Name: Budget Gap Assessment
Documentation: **Quantified funding gaps drive budget proposals.** The Budget Gap Assessment identifies differences between budgeted and required funding for approved initiatives, with gap amounts and drivers. It is issued after budget data has been compared against baseline and proposed commitments, meaning gaps are quantified and attributed. Budget change proposals are built directly from these quantified gaps, with amounts and offsets specified. This handover gives budget change drafting the gap amounts and the reasons behind each shortfall, so proposals address real funding needs.

Name: Budget Data Pack
Documentation: **A complete budget dataset** underpins gap assessment. When all budget inputs from accounting and planning records are collected and validated, the Budget Data Pack arrives with budgeted amounts, actuals, commitments, forecast positions, the period covered, and the source of each figure. This single consistent dataset lets gap assessment compare planned funding against actual and committed spending. The availability of these figures makes shortfall quantification possible and protects gap assessment from proceeding without actual and forecast amounts.

Name: Competency Data Set
Documentation: **Up-to-date skill baseline guides portfolio analysis.** The Competency Inventory lists each role, its required skills, current proficiency levels, and the date of last assessment. It is issued after current competency records have been collected from role profiles and assessments and checked for completeness, providing an up-to-date skill baseline. Training portfolio analysis uses the inventory to evaluate offerings against documented skill requirements and proficiency gaps. The handover ensures that analysis knows which skills are already present at which level, so evaluations target real gaps.

Name: Competency Data Set
Documentation: **Up-to-date skill baseline supports gap identification.** The Competency Inventory lists each role, its required skills, current proficiency levels, and the date of last assessment. It is issued after current competency records have been collected from role profiles and assessments and checked for completeness, providing an up-to-date skill baseline. Gap identification uses the inventory to detect discrepancies between required and current proficiency. The handover makes it possible to distinguish skills already mastered from missing ones, so gaps are identified accurately.

Name: Technology Data Set
Documentation: **A complete installation baseline** supports technology organisational analysis. After all technology assets are collected from configuration and asset records and validated, the Technology Data Set arrives listing installed applications, platforms, versions, support status, and ownership for each technology component. This complete inventory lets the analysis map items to business capabilities and identify duplication, coverage, and age. Its availability prevents the analysis from proceeding without the actual system landscape and ownership.

Name: Action Plan
Documentation: **An approved Action Plan authorises implementation.** The plan names selected actions, owners, milestones, resources assigned, and success measures for each initiative. It is issued after actions have been sequenced and approved against relevant assessments; its arrival means implementation work is authorised. This handover enables implementation to begin against the assigned owners, resources, and milestones. It protects against implementation assignments and schedules remaining unset, and no authorised sequence existing.

Name: Action Plan
Documentation: **Action Plan equips monitoring with measures.** For each initiative, the plan names selected actions, owners, milestones, resources assigned, and success measures. Issued after sequencing and approval, its arrival means monitoring work has defined measures for comparing actual progress. This handover enables monitoring to use the plan's success measures and milestones to compare actual progress against targets. It protects against monitoring having no defined measures or target dates to track.

Name: Action Plan
Documentation: **Action Plan supplies formal action list.** For each initiative, the plan names selected actions, owners, milestones, resources assigned, and success measures. Issued after sequencing and approval, its arrival means advisory publication has the formal action list. This handover enables advisory publication to use the planned actions and owners to communicate what is being done and why. It protects against advisory publication lacking the formal list of actions and responsible parties.

Name: Risk Register
Documentation: **Risk Register connects risks to actions.** The register records identified risks with likelihood, impact, owner, and current mitigation status. It is issued when risks have been captured as part of action planning and assigned owners; its arrival means the risk list is current and owned. This handover enables risk analysis to work from the owned risk entries and their assessed likelihood and impact. It protects against risk analysis not connecting risks to the actions that create them and proceeding without the current risk inventory.

Name: Budget Change Proposal
Documentation: **Proposed funding adjustments** are ready for consolidation. Once budget gaps become concrete changes and pass feasibility review, the Budget Change Proposal arrives with line-item amounts, justification, and expected effect on resource capacity. Final resource planning incorporates these adjustments into the overall allocation of funds and headcount. The presence of this proposal ensures final resource planning works from the adjusted funding levels it specifies rather than proceeding without those line-item changes.

Name: Competency Development Plan
Documentation: **Planned skill-building activities** are ready to be costed and scheduled. After competency gaps are matched to development actions and resources, the Competency Development Plan arrives listing target roles, delivery timing, and required trainers or materials. Final resource planning includes the people, time, and budget needed to execute these activities. The plan's availability ensures skill development capacity is included rather than omitted from resource finalisation. This keeps the final plan from underestimating the capacity required for competency development.

Name: Technology Architecture
Documentation: **The endorsed target architecture** sets the technology scope for planning. After technology gaps are translated into a confirmed future application, data, and integration structure, the Technology Architecture arrives with required platforms and migration steps. Final resource planning allocates budget and capacity for those platforms and the migration work described. The architecture's availability ensures resource finalisation funds the agreed technology scope rather than proceeding without the specific platforms and migration steps.

Name: Advisory Case
Documentation: **A documented issue and decision request** opens formal advisory work. When an advisory need is identified and the responsible owner accepts, the Advisory Case arrives stating the issue, affected parties, scope, and decision being sought. Formal advisory work begins with this defined issue and scope. The case's availability protects advisory initiation from lacking a documented issue or a clear decision request. This formal opening keeps the advisory focused on the stated issue and the requested decision.

Name: Competency Gap Report
Documentation: **Validated gap list guides portfolio analysis.** The Competency Gap Report lists the gaps between required and current skills, including affected roles and the size of each gap. It is issued after actual proficiency has been compared against requirements and discrepancies confirmed, providing a validated gap list. Training portfolio analysis uses the report to determine which training programmes address which gaps. The handover supplies the confirmed shortfall areas, so portfolio analysis matches programmes to real needs.

Name: Competency Gap Report
Documentation: **Validated gap list guides development planning.** The Competency Gap Report lists the gaps between required and current skills, including affected roles and the size of each gap. It is issued after actual proficiency has been compared against requirements and discrepancies confirmed, providing a validated gap list. Competency development planning builds activities from these role-specific gaps and their importance. The handover supplies the confirmed skill deficits to address, so development activities target real needs.

Name: Technology Gap Report
Documentation: The **Technology Gap Report details** the missing or inadequate technology capabilities, the business processes affected, and the expected impact of each gap. It is issued after the technology landscape has been compared with required capabilities and gaps have been confirmed. Its arrival means architecture work has a validated deficit list. This ensures technology architecture design addresses the confirmed capability gaps and their business impact, rather than proceeding without a validated list of deficits to close.

Name: Implementation Log
Documentation: **Implementation Log captures action completion** and records each completed action, including the date, owner, and any variance from the planned milestone or output. It is issued as actions are executed and their completion is recorded, so its arrival means the log carries the latest progress evidence. Monitoring effectiveness then compares these entries against the plan's milestones and measures to determine whether the actions are achieving their intended effect. Without the Implementation Log, monitoring has no evidence of execution progress.

Name: Implementation Log
Documentation: **Implementation Log supplies completion evidence** by recording each completed action, its date, owner, and any variance from the planned milestone or output. It is issued as actions are executed and their completion recorded, so its arrival means the log carries the latest progress evidence. Advisory publication then uses this completion evidence to report what has been done and which actions remain open. Without the Implementation Log, advisory publication lacks the record of executed work.

Name: Advisory Charter
Documentation: **Advisory Charter fixes scope and authority** by setting the advisory's purpose, scope, decision rights, and authorised limits for subsequent recommendations. It is issued once an advisory has been formally initiated and its mandate approved, so its arrival means the charter is binding on all subsequent work. Action planning then proceeds within these boundaries, ensuring recommendations and actions remain inside the approved scope and decision rights. Without the Advisory Charter, action planning lacks fixed scope and authority.

Name: Resource Assignment
Documentation: **Resource Assignment commits the people** by naming the individuals or teams allocated to each action, their time commitment, and the period of assignment. It is issued when advisory initiation has secured the necessary people and capacity, so its arrival means the named resources are committed to the work. Implementation then begins with these assigned people and their committed time, so actions are resourced from the start. Without the Resource Assignment, implementation lacks the allocated individuals and stalls.

Name: Effectiveness Review
Documentation: **Effectiveness Review delivers measured results** by documenting the advisory's action results against the original success measures, including variance and residual issues. It is issued after the monitoring period has produced sufficient evidence to assess outcomes, so its arrival means the results are available for a closure decision. The advisory is then closed using this outcome evidence, with residual issues recorded. Without the Effectiveness Review, the advisory closure proceeds without measured results.

Name: Effectiveness Review
Documentation: **Effectiveness Review provides outcome evidence** by documenting the measured results of the advisory's actions against the original success measures, including variance and residual issues. It is issued after the monitoring period has produced sufficient evidence to assess outcomes, so its arrival means the results are available for publication. Advisory publication then uses these measured results to inform stakeholders of what worked and what did not. Without the Effectiveness Review, publication lacks the outcome evidence and variance analysis.

Name: Technology Organizational Analysis
Documentation: The **Technology Organizational Assessment maps** each technology component to the capability it supports, its ownership, its age, and its coverage across requirements. It is issued after the technology inventory has been analysed against business capabilities, which means the assessment holds a full coverage map. This makes it possible for gap identification to compare required capabilities against the coverage map and find unsupported or poorly supported areas. It protects gap identification from proceeding without the analysed coverage and ownership context.

Name: Advisory Report
Documentation: The **Advisory Report consolidates** the findings, recommendations, actions taken, and measured results of the advisory into a final record. It is issued after the advisory has been published and all supporting material is complete, making it ready for archival and closure. This allows the advisory to be closed with a complete record of findings and results, and the report becomes the basis for any subsequent decision. It ensures closure does not happen without the consolidated record of the advisory's work.

Name: Project Order
Documentation: **Project Order authorizes billing** specifies the project deliverable, milestones, agreed pricing, billing schedule, and any customer-specific requirements. It is issued when the customer approves the proposal and the order is created with a valid project reference, so billing has a reliable project identifier. On arrival, billing uses the project milestones and pricing to schedule and issue invoices, ensuring the project has a billing schedule and does not remain unbilled.

Name: Project Order
Documentation: **Project Order drives packing** specifies the project deliverable, milestones, agreed pricing, billing schedule, and any customer-specific requirements. It is issued when the customer approves the proposal and the order is created with a valid project reference. On arrival, packing uses the project line items to prepare the required materials as specified. This ensures packing activity always has an order to pack against, preventing materials from being prepared without a customer-approved project context.

Name: Project Order
Documentation: **The approved Project Order** carries the project deliverable, milestones, agreed pricing, billing schedule, and any customer-specific requirements. It is issued once the customer approves the proposal and the order is created with a valid project reference. On arrival, picking uses the project line items to collect the required materials from inventory, giving pickers clear instructions for the project. This handover turns an approved proposal into clear picking instructions, ensuring the warehouse always knows what to gather.

Name: Project Order
Documentation: **Project Order provides staging context** specifies the project deliverable, milestones, agreed pricing, billing schedule, and any customer-specific requirements. It is issued when the customer approves the proposal and the order is created with a valid project reference. On arrival, inbound materials are received and staged according to the project's defined location and handling needs. This ensures staging has the project context needed to allocate materials rather than holding them without allocation.

Name: Project Order
Documentation: **Customer approval triggers a Project Order** that specifies the project deliverable, milestones, agreed pricing, billing schedule, and any customer-specific requirements. Once that order is created with a valid project reference, delivery and installation planning assigns dates and resources against the project milestones. This handover makes it possible to set a delivery window, so every customer receives a confirmed install date, and it protects against the absence of any delivery window or install date.

Name: Project Order
Documentation: **A customer-approved Project Order** specifies the project deliverable, milestones, agreed pricing, billing schedule, and any customer-specific requirements. When this order is created with a valid project reference, resource management allocates people and equipment to project tasks based on its requirements. This handover gives resource allocation a project basis, ensuring staffing is assigned rather than left unfilled. This protects against resource allocation lacking any project basis and staffing remaining unassigned.

Name: Project Order
Documentation: **Customer approval triggers a Project Order** that specifies the project deliverable, milestones, agreed pricing, billing schedule, and any customer-specific requirements. With this order in hand and a valid project reference, production uses the project specification and milestones to plan and execute the build. This handover gives production the project-specific work order it needs to produce the deliverable, protecting against a state where no such order exists and the deliverable never gets produced.

Name: Project Order
Documentation: **A customer-approved Project Order** specifies the project deliverable, milestones, agreed pricing, billing schedule, and any customer-specific requirements. When this order is created with a valid project reference, resource scheduling reserves the necessary capacity and assigns it to the project. This handover ensures capacity is reserved before the project begins, so the project does not compete with other work unprepared. This protects against capacity remaining unreserved and the project entering competition unprepared.

Name: Proposal
Documentation: **A Proposal details the solution,** pricing, delivery schedule, and contract terms offered to the customer, including scope and commitments. It is prepared after the customer opportunity is qualified and the solution is designed, reflecting all agreed requirements. Once the customer accepts the proposal, a project order is generated to begin delivery. This handover converts a qualified opportunity into a concrete order, so the proposed work is formally initiated and tracked.

Name: Proposal
Documentation: **A Proposal details the solution,** pricing, delivery schedule, and contract terms offered to the customer, including scope and timeline commitments. It is prepared after the customer opportunity is qualified and the solution is designed. Resource planning uses the proposal's scope and timeline to tentatively reserve capacity as a preliminary plan for the proposed work. This handover ensures a resource forecast exists before the work is assigned, protecting the schedule from unplanned capacity gaps and last-minute shortages.

Name: Invoice
Documentation: **Invoice for delivered shipment or service** states the amount due, payment terms, invoice number, line items, quantities, and the reference to the fulfilled order or shipment. It is issued after the related shipment or service has been delivered and all billing terms are met. When it arrives, payment approval reviews the invoice against the purchase order or contract and schedules payment, clearing the way for the supplier to be paid and ensuring the supplier balance does not remain open.

Name: Load Manifest
Documentation: **Load Manifest lists** every shipment loaded on the vehicle, with piece counts, weights, and destination references. It is generated once loading finishes and the cargo matches the shipping schedule. On arrival, the carrier uses the manifest for regulatory checks and the handover record. A complete manifest is what lets the vehicle depart on time: it consolidates the cargo details into a single document, avoiding any hold while the shipment is reconciled.

Name: Load Manifest
Documentation: **Load Manifest lists** every shipment loaded on the vehicle, with piece counts, weights, and destination references. It is generated once loading finishes and the cargo matches the shipping schedule. On arrival, the carrier uses the manifest for regulatory checks and the handover record. A complete manifest is what lets the vehicle depart on time: it consolidates the cargo details into a single document, avoiding any hold while the shipment is reconciled.

Name: Packing Slip
Documentation: **A Packing Slip accompanies every package.** Generated at the completion of packing, it travels with the physical package and lists each package's item numbers, quantities, and any special handling instructions. At loading, this document allows the loader to reconcile cartons against the load plan. That item-level check is what catches misloads before a carton goes to the wrong destination. Keeping the Packing Slip in the flow protects against misloads going unnoticed.

Name: Packing Slip
Documentation: **A Packing Slip verifies carrier handover.** Generated at the completion of packing, it travels with the physical package and lists each package's item numbers, quantities, and any special handling instructions. At shipment, the list is used to confirm counts and conditions before the carrier accepts the shipment. This handover ensures the carrier receives a manifest of contents and gives both parties the item-level record needed to resolve any later dispute.

Name: Packing Slip
Documentation: **A Packing Slip accompanies every package.** Produced when packing is complete, it travels with the physical package and lists item numbers, quantities, and any special handling instructions for each package. At loading, the loader uses this list to reconcile cartons against the load plan. The handover matters because it provides the item-level check that catches misloads before they leave the dock. Keeping this document in the flow prevents carton errors from going unnoticed.

Name: Pick List
Documentation: **Picked items make packing possible.** The physical goods retrieved from inventory carry SKU, quantity, lot or serial number, and the order reference. They arrive when the picker confirms each line on the pick list and the correct quantity is collected. Packing then matches these items to the order lines and begins to prepare the shipment. This handover supplies the physical units that packing needs, preventing the order from remaining unpacked.

Name: Pick List
Documentation: **A Pick List directs** the collection of items for one or more orders, specifying locations, quantities, and the order line reference. It is issued once inventory has been reserved and the picking wave is released, signalling that the picker can begin. The picker then retrieves the listed items from the designated storage locations. Having the Pick List in hand gives the picker exactly what to collect, so the order keeps moving rather than sitting idle.

Name: Pick List
Documentation: **A Pick List directs** the collection of items for one or more orders, specifying locations, quantities, and the order line reference. It is issued once inventory has been reserved and the picking wave is released, signalling that the picker can begin. The picker then retrieves the listed items from the designated storage locations. Having the Pick List in hand gives the picker exactly what to collect, so the order keeps moving rather than sitting idle.

Name: Staging Record
Documentation: **Staging location record** carries the storage bay, aisle and shelf identifier, the item number, quantity, receipt batch or lot, and the time the goods were placed there. It is issued when received goods pass inspection and are placed in a staging area, signaling that the items are physically present at the named location and available for picking. Pickers then retrieve the items from that stated location in the sequence required by open pick lists, so picking begins with a confirmed location instead of a search through storage areas.

Name: Proposal Brief
Documentation: **Proposal Brief with agreed scope** carries the customer's stated requirements, evaluation criteria, submission deadline, budget or pricing constraints, and any conditions attached to the request. It is issued when the received request is assessed as a genuine opportunity and all required details are extracted and validated. Its arrival means proposal development starts from an agreed scope. The proposal content is then prepared directly against these stated criteria and commercial constraints. This ensures the proposal team works from confirmed customer needs rather than assumptions.

Name: Delivery & Installation Schedule
Documentation: **The Delivery & Installation Schedule commits** planned delivery dates, installation time slots, customer locations, order line items, required equipment, and the sequence of departures. It is issued when delivery and installation capacity is reserved and the customer confirms the proposed slot, so load planning proceeds against committed dates. With it in place, docks and trucks are sequenced according to departure times and routes, and orders are staged in dispatch order instead of waiting in an unsorted pile.

Name: Delivery & Installation Schedule
Documentation: **The Delivery & Installation Schedule sequences** the pick operation by carrying committed delivery dates, customer locations, order line items, and the stop sequence for scheduled departures. It is issued once delivery and installation slots are confirmed and departures are scheduled, giving the pick operation a dated and sequenced requirement. With this schedule, pick lists are completed in the order needed for each scheduled departure and customer stop, so picking stays synchronised with the delivery sequence and staged orders do not wait for departure.

Name: Delivery & Installation Schedule
Documentation: **The Delivery & Installation Schedule fixes** departure times, routing, assigned vehicle, customer stops, and the items loaded for each stop. It is issued when delivery and installation resource assignments are confirmed and the route is fixed, so dispatch execution can start from a committed departure plan. With this schedule, vehicles are released against the scheduled departures and each shipment is confirmed against its stop, ensuring that shipments always have a route and stop assignment before they leave.

Name: Resource Schedule
Documentation: **The Resource Schedule confirms** resource identifiers, skill or equipment types, availability windows, assigned task or project, and the quantity of each resource assigned. It is issued when project resource requirements are balanced against current capacity and conflicts are resolved, so slot scheduling proceeds with confirmed resource availability. With this schedule, delivery and installation slots are reserved using the assigned resources and their availability windows, preventing double-booking.

Name: Resource Schedule
Documentation: **The Resource Schedule assigns** resource identifiers, task identifiers, availability windows, and quantity commitments for the assigned project resources. It is issued when resource assignments are confirmed and no capacity conflicts remain, giving resource issue a specific project and task to draw from. With this schedule, resources are issued to the assigned tasks in the stated quantities and at the stated times, so nothing is handed out without a project assignment or timing instruction.

Name: Resource Schedule
Documentation: **The Resource Schedule details** labour, equipment and material assignments with the production task, start time, and quantity required. It is issued when project resource requirements are balanced and production tasks are scheduled, so production receives the specific resource assignment for each task. With this schedule, production consumes the assigned resources as scheduled and records their use against the task, ensuring that tasks always have designated resources and never compete for unassigned capacity.

Name: Shipment
Documentation: **Shipment record enables receiving checks** The Shipment record carries the shipped item numbers, quantities, the packaging identifiers, carrier reference, and the originating order or delivery number. It is issued when goods leave the shipping point and the carrier accepts them. With this record, receiving can allocate dock space and check the incoming goods against the shipment record, so inbound goods arrive with a reference for count and their condition checks.

Name: Shipment
Documentation: **Shipment record gives invoicing confirmed quantities** The Shipment record carries actual shipped quantities, item identifiers, carrier reference, and dispatch date. It is issued when the carrier accepts the goods and the shipped quantities are recorded. With this record, invoicing has the actual quantities that left and can produce a customer invoice from the shipped quantities and dispatch information, so invoicing does not lack confirmation and does not wait for shipment data.

Name: Shipment Notification
Documentation: **Shipment Notification starts invoicing on dispatch** A Shipment Notification carries the tracking number, carrier, dispatch date, expected delivery date, item list, and quantity for a dispatched shipment. It is issued when the carrier takes possession and shipment details are confirmed. Its arrival means the customer and internal invoicing are advised that the shipment is on its way. With this notification, invoicing can prepare the customer invoice on dispatch immediately, rather than waiting for shipment confirmation before it begins.

Name: Shipment Notification
Documentation: **Shipment Notification provides inquiry reference** This notice carries the tracking number, carrier, dispatch date, expected delivery date, item list, and quantity for the dispatched shipment. It is issued at dispatch and is available as soon as the carrier accepts the shipment. Inquiry handling can use this reference to answer shipment status questions using the tracking and expected delivery details, so customers get a shipment reference instead of no information at all.

Name: Shipment Notification
Documentation: **Shipment Notification gives receiving advance notice** This notice carries the shipment identifier, item count, packaging, carrier, expected arrival date, and unloading requirements. It is issued when the shipment is dispatched and the carrier provides the arrival estimate. With this notice, receiving can prepare dock capacity, staffing, and handling equipment for the incoming shipment, so the shipment does not arrive unannounced at the dock and receiving is not left without advance preparation.

Name: Proof of Delivery
Documentation: **Signed proof of delivery** carries the receiver's signature, delivery date and time, delivered item list, quantities, and any noted damage or shortage. It is issued when the receiver signs and accepts the shipment at the delivery location, confirming that the goods are delivered and accepted. This signed proof is what settlement uses to proceed, providing confirmation of receipt and acceptance. That confirmation keeps payment from remaining blocked by giving settlement the evidence it needs.

Name: Proof of Delivery
Documentation: **Signed proof of delivery** carries the signed receipt, delivery date, items, quantities, and exception notes for the delivered shipment. It is issued when the shipment is accepted and signed for at the destination, confirming delivery for the invoice. Invoicing finalises the customer invoice using this signed proof, attaching it as the delivery confirmation. This confirmation is what allows the invoice to be closed rather than left open while delivery verification is pending.

Name: Process Performance Analysis
Documentation: **Process Performance Analysis quantifies performance deviations** Capturing process cycle times, throughput, error rates, and constraint locations with comparisons against targets, it issues after process flow data analysis identifies deviations. On arrival, assessment of business rule changes uses these deviations and constraints to determine which rules cause delays or errors. This handover ensures rules assessment has a measured performance basis, protecting it from lacking the quantified diagnostic picture needed for rule change decisions.

Name: Process Performance Analysis
Documentation: **Process Performance Analysis captures** measured cycle times, throughput, error rates, and constraint locations against targets. It is issued after process flow data has been analysed and performance deviations from targets are identified, delivering a quantified, diagnostic performance picture. This handover gives technology change assessment the concrete performance constraints and error locations it needs to identify where technology change is warranted. With measured performance evidence in hand, technology assessment evaluates actual gaps rather than assumptions, so change proposals are tied to observed process weaknesses.

Name: Process Performance Analysis
Documentation: **Process Performance Analysis supplies** cycle times, throughput, error rates, and constraint locations compared against targets. It is produced after process flow data has been analysed and deviations identified, giving solution definition a measured problem statement. With these performance gaps and constraints, solution definition targets specific process changes rather than generic improvements. The handover ensures that process solutions are built from observed performance shortfalls, so each change addresses a diagnosed constraint or error location.

Name: Process Standardization Analysis
Documentation: The **Process Standardization Analysis compares** process variants across units, identifying differences in steps, roles, and outputs. It is issued only after process flows have been compared and commonalities and variations have been documented, which means the standardisation picture is complete. This complete picture is what allows process solutions to consolidate variants and reduce duplication, using the standardisation findings as their basis. The handover therefore ensures that solution definition does not proceed without the variation map.

Name: Network Analysis
Documentation: The **Supply Chain Network Analysis records** the location, capacity, and flow patterns of facilities, suppliers, and customers, plus associated lead times and costs. It is issued after the network structure and flows have been modelled and validated, which means the network baseline is available for solution design. This baseline is what process solutions use to address capacity, handoff, and lead time issues across the network. The handover ensures solution definition does not proceed without the network flow and capacity baseline.

Name: Process Solution
Documentation: **Process Solution sets the change direction** by specifying the recommended changes to process steps, roles, controls, and handoffs, together with expected performance effect. It is issued after solution alternatives have been evaluated and a preferred solution selected, so its arrival means the solution is specified and ready for detailed design. To-be process design then elaborates this selected solution into detailed future process steps and responsibilities. Without the Process Solution, detailed to-be design lacks the selected direction.

Name: Process Solution
Documentation: **Process Solution enables portfolio grouping** by specifying the recommended changes to process steps, roles, controls, and handoffs, together with expected performance effect. It is issued after solution alternatives have been evaluated and a preferred solution selected, so its arrival means the solution is specified and ready for portfolio grouping. The process change portfolio then groups these selected solutions into a change list with dependencies and expected benefits. Without the Process Solution, the portfolio lacks the solution content to group.

Name: To-Be Process
Documentation: **A fully designed To-Be Process** arrives once the selected process solution is elaborated into a complete future process definition. It carries the future process steps, roles, inputs, outputs, and control points. This arrival enables portfolio aggregation to include fully designed future processes and their change scope. The process change portfolio remains complete with detailed future process content, so planning proceeds with a specified future state rather than an undefined set of changes.

Name: To-Be Process
Documentation: **A fully designed To-Be Process** moves into validation once the selected solution has been elaborated into a complete future process definition. It provides the future process steps, roles, inputs, outputs, and control points that validation checks for feasibility and completeness. This handover gives the validation work the exact specification it needs to test the designed process, protecting against feasibility gaps and incomplete process definitions. The validation effort therefore examines the actual to-be state rather than an assumed or partial one.

Name: Process Change Portfolio
Documentation: The **Process Change Portfolio contains** the approved set of process changes, grouped by business area, with owners, timing, and expected benefits. It is issued after to-be processes and solutions have been consolidated into a coordinated change set and approved, which means the portfolio is final and ready for communication. This final portfolio makes the approved change set visible to all affected parties upon publication. It ensures communication of process changes does not happen without the consolidated, approved list.

Name: Process Flow
Documentation: **The Process Flow documents** the sequence of activities, decisions, and handoffs in a process, including roles and systems used at each step. It is issued when a process has been documented and its flow validated against actual operations. Its arrival provides performance analysis with a reliable baseline for locating timing, queues, and error-prone handoffs. That baseline is the structural map against which performance is measured. This handover ensures performance analysis has this structural map, so it sees where timing, queues, or handoffs fail instead of lacking that visibility.

Name: Process Flow
Documentation: **The Process Flow Map records** each process step, its inputs and outputs, decision points, and responsible roles, carrying the current-state sequence that standardization work compares across variants. It is issued only after the current process is documented from trigger to outcome. Its arrival gives standardization analysis a complete as-is flow and a shared reference model for comparison. That comparison exposes duplicate and divergent steps. This handover provides the common representation that makes inconsistent process variants visible and correctable, rather than leaving them uncorrected.

Name: Process Flow
Documentation: **The Process Flow Map records** each process step, handoff, decision point, and responsible role, carrying the end-to-end sequence that network analysis needs to trace how work moves across locations and systems. It is issued only after the current process is documented from trigger to outcome. Its arrival provides the as-is process connectivity that network analysis uses to map process nodes and handoffs onto physical and organizational locations, revealing where flow is absent or duplicated. This handover ensures network analysis has the connectivity needed to reveal dependencies across network nodes, so those dependencies do not remain unknown.

Name: Process Flow
Documentation: **The Process Flow Map records** each process step, business rule trigger, exception path, and decision point, carrying the exact locations where rules act on work. It is issued only after the current process is documented from trigger to outcome. Its arrival gives rule change assessment the complete set of decision points and rule sites, so each business rule is assessed against its process location. That isolates which rules change when a step changes. This handover ensures assessment does not work from fragments or memory, and that no decision point is overlooked or affected rule missed.

Name: Process Flow
Documentation: **Process Flow Map role-to-step structure** records each process step, its responsible role, and the organizational unit that performs it. Issued only after the current process is documented from trigger to outcome, this map makes current role assignments visible for change assessment. Its arrival allows every position touched by a process change to be identified, so responsibility impacts are assigned to the correct organizational unit. It protects against guessed role impacts and changes being assigned to the wrong units or left unassigned.

Name: Process Flow
Documentation: **Process Flow Map system touchpoints** records each process step, the systems and interfaces used, and data passed between them. Issued only after the current process is documented from trigger to outcome, the map makes as-is system touchpoints available for change assessment. Arrival triggers assessment of each system interaction against the process flow, exposing which interfaces are affected by technology change. It protects against starting from a system inventory rather than actual flow, so unused or missing integration points are not overlooked.

Name: Process Flow
Documentation: **Process Flow Map provides agreed baseline** records the current process step sequence, decision points, roles, and handoffs. Issued only after the current process is documented from trigger to outcome, it makes a verified current state available as the baseline for future design. This allows direct editing of the baseline to produce to-be process definitions, ensuring changes are recorded against an agreed current state. It protects against design without an agreed current state, so omissions from the current process do not carry forward unchecked.

Name: Process Flow
Documentation: **Process Flow Map activity-to-role structure** delivers each process step, its responsible role, and the organizational unit that performs it. Issued only after the current process is documented from trigger to outcome, it makes as-is process steps and roles available for organizational analysis. This allows accountable positions to be mapped to process steps, producing a responsibility structure for the current process. It protects against responsibility gaps by ensuring organizational analysis can connect activities to accountable positions.

Name: Process Organizational Analysis
Documentation: **Process Organizational Analysis details current responsibilities** for each process step, accountable role, required skills, and organizational unit. It arrives only after current-state process maps are reconciled with role and skill data, so the process-to-role alignment is documented and ready for change assessment. This enables change assessment to use precise responsibility impacts per process step, building the organizational change list from actual gaps. The change assessment avoids relying on generic role descriptions and keeps process-specific roles affected by change identified.

Name: Process Organizational Analysis
Documentation: **Process Organizational Analysis provides accountability baseline** for each process step, accountable role, required skills, and organizational unit. It is issued after current-state process maps are reconciled with role and skill data, so the existing responsibility structure is available for to-be design. This enables to-be process design to incorporate current role assignments and specify role changes where process steps change. To-be design thus works from a verified accountability baseline instead of inheriting unverified role assignments for new processes.

Name: Validation Report
