Documentation: The **Validation Report records** the outcome of checking each proposed to-be process against design criteria, constraints, and stakeholder sign-off. It carries the determination of whether each change is fit to proceed. It is issued only after proposed processes are validated and the outcomes are recorded, which means a set of validated change candidates is ready for portfolio assembly. This ensures portfolio construction includes only validated changes and excludes unvalidated proposals from planning. It protects the change portfolio from being formed from unvetted proposals, preventing invalid or infeasible changes from entering planning.

Name: Market Priority Analysis
Documentation: The **Market Priority Analysis ranks** market segments, demand trends, and competitive requirements by strategic importance. It carries the ordered set of external priorities that capabilities must serve. It is issued only after market signals are assessed and priorities are ordered, which means demand-side priorities are available to guide capability identification. This ensures capability identification evaluates gaps and strengths in order of market relevance, rather than proceeding without market context. It protects against capabilities being selected for internal reasons instead of required outcomes.

Name: Benchmark Report
Documentation: **Benchmark Report quantifies performance gaps** across cost, speed, service, and asset efficiency against external peers or targets. It is issued only after performance data is normalized and comparisons are completed, signalling that the external performance baseline is ready for strategy development. When the report arrives, strategy work sets objectives relative to benchmark positions: quantified gaps anchor targets to real external reference rather than inward-looking assumptions. This handover makes target setting grounded in actual competitive position, protecting against arbitrary objectives.

Name: Scorecard
Documentation: **The Scorecard defines measurable targets** for supply chain performance, including metrics and thresholds. It arrives after performance dimensions and measurement definitions are set, giving strategy development an agreed performance yardstick. This enables strategy work to align objectives with defined metrics and assess strategic choices against scorecard impact. Strategy development thus expresses objectives as measurable targets, avoiding the absence of a performance yardstick.

Name: Scorecard
Documentation: **Scorecard specifies metrics needing ownership** along with targets and thresholds for supply chain performance. It arrives after performance dimensions and measurement definitions are set, so metrics requiring ownership are available for organizational analysis. This enables the organizational analysis to map metric ownership and data stewardship, assigning an accountable role to each metric. The metric organizational analysis therefore works from defined metrics, ensuring ownership is not left unmapped.

Name: Supply Chain Network
Documentation: **Supply Chain Network names** every node, lane, flow, and relationship in the current structure. It is issued after the current supply chain structure is defined and agreed, making the actual footprint available for strategy development. Strategy work uses this concrete network as its evaluation base, so each option is tested against existing nodes and lanes rather than an abstract model. With the handover in place, strategy development is grounded in the real network footprint and proposals respect actual constraints instead of ignoring them.

Name: Supply Chain Network
Documentation: **Supply Chain Network provides** the nodes, lanes, flows, and relationships that make up the operating backbone. Issued after the current structure is defined and agreed, it gives capability identification the structural elements needed to link each capability to specific flows. Capability identification proceeds with the network as its operating backbone, so every identified capability is tied to particular nodes and flows. The handover protects against capabilities being defined in isolation; with the network in hand, capability roles are grounded in the actual spatial and flow structure.

Name: Supply Chain Network
Documentation: **Supply Chain Network delineates** the nodes, lanes, flows, and relationships that form the current structure. Issued after the current supply chain structure is defined and agreed, it supplies the structural elements for which ownership is assigned. Organizational analysis uses these elements to locate responsibility for nodes and lanes, so accountability for flows becomes explicit. The handover ensures that every network element has a clear owner, preventing accountability gaps across the supply chain.

Name: Supply Chain Strategy
Documentation: **Supply Chain Strategy sets official direction** for planning and execution once strategic objectives and initiatives are approved. It records approved objectives, priorities, initiatives, and resource implications. This handover enables publication of the strategy to all affected parties, making it the formal directive. The organization therefore moves forward with an approved strategy rather than continuing on prior direction.

Name: Supply Chain Strategy
Documentation: **Supply Chain Strategy enables consistency analysis** once strategic objectives and initiatives are approved. It carries the approved objectives, priorities, initiatives, and resource implications as consolidated strategy content. This handover allows the analysis work to test strategy consistency and completeness, detecting conflicts between objectives and constraints. The strategy analysis therefore uses the approved content rather than working from drafts or fragments.

Name: Discovered Supply Chains
Documentation: **Discovered Supply Chains catalog identifies** each supply chain with its products, customers, channels, and demand patterns. It is issued only after discovery has identified distinct supply chain instances, signalling that the full population is ready for segmentation. When the catalog arrives, segmentation groups the discovered set into segments by shared operating characteristics, assigning each chain to a segment. This population makes grouping concrete: segmentation works on actual chains rather than defining segments in the abstract, ensuring every chain receives a segment assignment.

Name: Inquiry Response
Documentation: **Inquiry Response marks inquiry answered** and carries the solution, terms, and supporting documentation delivered to the requester. The response arrives only after the solution has been distributed, signalling that no further action is pending. Once the response is delivered, the inquiry record closes and is removed from open workload. This completion clears the service request from the queue: delivering the response prevents unanswered inquiries from accumulating in the backlog and keeps the workload current.

Name: Solution Candidate
Documentation: **Solution Candidate matches customer need** to an available offering or service. It is issued only when a possible solution is identified and deemed suitable for presentation, signalling that a presentable answer exists. When the candidate arrives, presentation work structures it into a customer-facing response. This fit is what gives the response its content: with a candidate, the inquiry moves out of solution identification and into a prepared answer, avoiding stalling in search mode.

Name: Inquiry Response Draft
Documentation: **Inquiry Response Draft carries approved content** ready for final review and delivery. It is issued only after a solution candidate is formatted and approved for distribution, signalling that the draft is complete and awaiting delivery. When the draft arrives, distribution sends the response to the requester through the appropriate channel, and the draft becomes the Inquiry Response upon delivery. This approved content is what distribution uses to proceed: with the draft available, the inquiry moves out of presentation and into the customer's hands, avoiding a stall at the preview stage.

Name: Segmented Supply Chains
Documentation: **Segmented Supply Chains classify each chain** into groups based on shared operating characteristics such as demand pattern, service requirement, and cost profile. The classification is issued only after discovered supply chains are segmented, signalling that each chain has a segment assignment available for prioritization. When it arrives, prioritization ranks supply chains by segment and directs resources to segments with the highest strategic value. This segment assignment makes ranking possible: prioritization works on differentiated groups rather than treating all chains as an undifferentiated set.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record carries full routing context**. Every received inquiry is captured as an Inquiry Record containing the requester, topic, channel, urgency, and timestamp. Once the record is issued at logging, its arrival signals that the inquiry is ready for routing. That triggers assignment to the appropriate handling queue based on inquiry category and service type, placing the inquiry in the correct workstream. This handover ensures no routing decision is missed, so inquiries do not remain unassigned in the intake inbox.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record supplies demand evidence**. When an inquiry is received and logged, the Inquiry Record captures the requester, topic, channel, urgency, and timestamp. Its arrival makes direct customer interest signals available for business plan analysis. Those signals allow planning assumptions to reflect actual inquiry volume and topic instead of relying on external estimates. The handover protects business plan analysis from missing direct demand evidence and keeps planning aligned with expressed customer interest.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record provides market input**. When an inquiry is received and logged, the Inquiry Record captures the requester, topic, channel, urgency, and timestamp. Its arrival makes direct market input available for competitive landscape analysis, revealing competitor mentions, unmet needs, and churn triggers. That allows competitor movements and unmet needs to be identified from actual customer contacts instead of being inferred from secondary sources. This handover keeps competitive analysis grounded in direct market evidence.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record provides demand weighting**. When an inquiry is received and logged, the Inquiry Record captures the requester, topic, channel, urgency, and timestamp. Its arrival makes actual inquiry demand available as a weighting factor for strategic market priority analysis. That allows high-inquiry areas to gain priority based on direct customer demand evidence. The handover keeps strategic market priorities aligned with expressed customer needs, preventing priorities from being set without that demand signal.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record supplies benchmark inputs**. When an inquiry is received and logged, the Inquiry Record captures the requester, topic, channel, urgency, and timestamp. Its arrival makes customer-facing performance signals available for supply chain benchmarking, including inquiry response times and requested capabilities. That enables benchmark comparison to measure service-related gaps based on actual customer inquiry signals. The handover ensures these signals are included, so performance gaps tied to service inquiries appear in benchmark results rather than being missed.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record carries closure classification**. When an inquiry is received and logged, the Inquiry Record captures the requester, topic, channel, urgency, and timestamp, along with the classification that determines whether immediate closure is appropriate. For an informational inquiry, its arrival closes the record immediately, engaging no handling queue and removing the request from open workload. This handover ensures informational inquiries do not remain open and consume intake capacity, as the closure trigger is built in.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record feeds data collection**. When an inquiry is received and logged, the Inquiry Record captures the requester, topic, channel, urgency, and timestamp. Its arrival triggers collection of supply chain data by logging these inquiry details into datasets. That ensures customer-facing demand and issue signals populate the data stores, keeping the supply chain dataset complete. The handover prevents data collection from missing these signals and leaving gaps in the dataset.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record provides service measures**. When an inquiry is received and logged, the Inquiry Record captures the requester, topic, channel, urgency, and timestamp. Its arrival triggers scorecard definition with inquiry volume and resolution speed as candidate metrics. That ensures customer experience measures are represented in the scorecard. The handover prevents scorecard definition from lacking service inquiry measures, so customer experience metrics are not underrepresented in the final scorecard; these measures come directly from the logged inquiry records.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record delivers customer geography** for network definition. Every inquiry is logged with its requester, topic, channel, urgency, and timestamp, and the record carries the inquiry locations and requested delivery points. When the record arrives, network definition uses those geographic demand signals directly. This allows node placement to reflect actual customer geography rather than relying on assumptions.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record delivers customer inquiry evidence** for strategy development. Each record captures the requester, topic, channel, urgency, and timestamp, and carries the themes and demand patterns that emerge from the inquiry. When an inquiry is received and logged, the record arrives with that evidence. Strategy development then uses these themes and patterns as direct input, ensuring strategic priorities reflect what customers actually asked for. This keeps customer needs represented in the strategy rather than overlooked.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record reveals supply chains** through customer attributes. The record captures the requester, topic, channel, urgency, and timestamp, and specifically carries the requester, product, and location attributes that link to known supply chains. When an inquiry is received and logged, these attributes become available for supply chain discovery. By linking inquiry attributes to known chains, the discovery process surfaces new or unrecognized supply chains that only appear through customer inquiries. This ensures discovery does not miss chains revealed solely by inquiry data.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record enables response delivery** to the correct requester. The record captures the requester, topic, channel, urgency, and timestamp, and specifically carries the contact and channel details needed for delivery. When an inquiry is received and logged, the record arrives with the original inquiry context. Solution distribution then uses those contact and channel details to send the prepared response to the right person. This ensures the response reaches the correct requester instead of being lost or misdirected.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record is the search key** for solution matching. The record captures the requester, topic, channel, urgency, and timestamp, and it carries the customer's exact need. When an inquiry is received and logged, that need becomes available as the search key. Solution identification then matches the inquiry details against available offerings. This allows matching to begin from the customer's stated need, not from an assumption of what they want.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record exposes capability gaps** driven by customer demand. The record captures the requester, topic, channel, urgency, and timestamp, and carries the inquiry-driven capability gaps revealed by repeated customer requests. When an inquiry is received and logged, this customer demand signal becomes available for capability identification. Capability identification then uses these gaps to surface missing capabilities that would otherwise be identified only internally. This ensures customer demand directly shapes the strategic capability agenda.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record enables metric ownership** assignment. The record captures the requester, topic, channel, urgency, and timestamp, and carries inquiry handling data as the subject for metric ownership. When an inquiry is received and logged, these inquiry metrics become available for organizational analysis. The analysis then uses this data to assign ownership of inquiry-related metrics. This ensures that responsibility for service measures is clearly mapped rather than left unassigned.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record maps inquiry touchpoints** for organizational analysis. The record captures the requester, topic, channel, urgency, and timestamp, and carries inquiry handling responsibilities and locations. When an inquiry is received and logged, these touchpoints become available for supply chain organizational analysis. The analysis then uses this input to assign ownership of inquiry-related supply chain activities. This ensures customer inquiry touchpoints are not missed and response handling responsibility is clearly assigned.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record carries complete requester context.** Logged with enough detail to act on and assigned a unique identifier, it holds the requester identity, stated need, desired outcome, response deadline, and channel of first contact. It arrives ready for response preparation without further intake work. Its arrival causes solution alternatives to be assembled for the requester, creating a response path and giving the requester options that otherwise would not exist.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record drives supply chain prioritisation.** Once logged with enough detail to act on and assigned a unique identifier, the record carries requester identity, stated need, desired outcome, response deadline, and channel of first contact. It arrives ready for prioritisation work. Its arrival causes supply chains to be ranked by relevance to the inquiry and by the level of demand or risk the inquiry exposes, creating the basis for ordering which supply chains require attention first.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record enables supply chain segmentation.** Once logged with enough detail to act on and assigned a unique identifier, the record carries requester identity, stated need, desired outcome, response deadline, and channel of first contact. It arrives ready for segmentation work. Its arrival causes supply chains to be assigned to segments using the inquiry's product, service, location, or volume attributes, ensuring the inquiry's demand signal is included and its requirements are not omitted.

Name: Inquiry Record
Documentation: **Inquiry Record enables reassignment with context.** Once logged with enough detail to act on and assigned a unique identifier, it carries the requester identity, stated need, desired outcome, response deadline, and channel of first contact. It arrives ready for reassignment. Its arrival causes the inquiry to be handed to another handling group with the original context and attachments preserved, ensuring the inquiry does not remain stuck in the originating queue and reassignment actually occurs.

Name: Request Assessment
Documentation: **Pricing needs a sound basis.** A **Request Assessment** records the request scope, item specifications, quantities, required delivery or service dates, and any commercial constraints affecting pricing. It is issued after the request is reviewed and determined actionable, with all mandatory fields completed, arriving only when the request is clear enough for price selection. Its arrival causes a priced list to be assembled from standard rates and current cost positions, and ensures price selection has an approved request basis from which to compile an offer.

Name: Request Assessment
Documentation: **Proposal drafting depends on verified details.** A **Request Assessment** records the request scope, item specifications, quantities, required delivery or service dates, and any commercial constraints affecting proposal development. It is issued after the request is reviewed and determined actionable, with all mandatory fields completed, arriving only when the request is clear enough for proposal drafting. Its arrival causes a proposal draft to be built using the assessed scope and constraints, giving proposal drafting the verified request details it needs to produce a draft.

Name: Negotiated Terms
Documentation: **Negotiated Terms capture agreed commercial points** including price, payment terms, delivery obligations, liability caps, and any accepted concessions. They are issued only when the parties reach provisional agreement on all negotiable points and the terms are recorded without open items, arriving ready for formal execution. Once the terms are in hand, signature pages are prepared and authorised signatories are collected. This agreement snapshot is what makes the signing event possible, protecting against the agreement remaining unexecuted.

Name: Signed Standard Terms
Documentation: **Signed Standard Terms carry executed authority** with the signature, date, and authority of the signing party attached. They are issued when all required signatures are applied to the standard terms document and the signing authority is verified, arriving as a legally executed standard agreement. Once these signed terms are present, a contract instance is released based on those terms. This execution is what triggers the contract release, protecting against standard terms remaining unexecuted.

Name: Standard Contract Terms
Documentation: **Standard contract terms establish baseline** when a contract on standard terms is released and available for reuse. These pre-approved clauses, commercial conditions, and compliance obligations form the authoritative baseline for all proposal development. Proposals built on the standard template proceed directly on these terms without renegotiating base clauses. This handover protects proposal drafting from lacking an approved contractual anchor and from redefining terms from scratch; the released terms become the single source for proposal work.

Name: Renewal Request
Documentation: **Renewal drafting needs a formal trigger.** A **Renewal Request** carries the current contract identifier, expiry date, renewal intent, requested changes, and any updated commercial or scope requirements from the receiving party. It is issued when a party formally requests continuation or modification of an existing contract and provides the necessary details, arriving ready for renewal drafting. Its arrival causes renewal terms to be drafted from the existing contract and the requested changes, ensuring renewal drafting has a trigger and the contract gains a successor before expiry.

Name: Renewal Request
Documentation: **Scheduling a renewal requires clear intent.** A **Renewal Request** carries the current contract identifier, expiry date, renewal intent, requested changes, and any updated commercial or scope requirements from the receiving party. It is issued when a party formally requests continuation or modification of an existing contract and provides the necessary details, arriving ready for scheduling. Its arrival causes a renewal activity to be scheduled with owners, dates, and review steps, ensuring the contract's expiry is handled through a planned renewal rather than left unplanned.

Name: Renewal Proposal
Documentation: **Complete renewal proposal enables negotiation** once it has been drafted and internally reviewed. It packages the proposed renewal terms, pricing, scope changes, and the rationale for each departure from the expiring contract. This consolidated position becomes the formal basis for negotiation. It allows the parties to open discussions on the renewal terms directly, rather than trying to piece together an informal picture. Without this consolidated renewal position, formal negotiation cannot start.

Name: Draft Renewal Agreement
Documentation: **Presentation-ready draft renewal agreement** emerges when negotiation produces a draft complete enough to show the receiving party for acceptance. It holds the negotiated renewal terms in contract form, with clauses marked as agreed or outstanding. This handover allows the draft agreement to be presented for internal or external approval, turning informal negotiation notes into a formal renewal offer. The movement ensures a formal renewal offer is available for approval rather than leaving negotiated terms in scattered notes.

Name: Approved Renewal Agreement
Documentation: **Approved renewal agreement ready for execution** arrives only after the presented renewal receives approval from designated approvers. It carries the final renewal terms along with the approval of the presenting authority and any required internal endorsements. This handover triggers signature collection on the approved renewal. Signature collection can begin immediately, allowing the renewal to move toward execution rather than leaving the expiring contract in force. The approved terms become the basis for collecting all required signatures.

Name: Signed Renewal Agreement
Documentation: **Signed renewal agreement becomes legally binding** when the agreement is fully signed and the signing authority is verified. It carries the executed renewal terms with all signatures and dates required to make the renewal enforceable. This handover triggers an update to the contract record, moving it to the new term and new expiry date. The executed amendment ensures the renewal is in force rather than leaving the contract on its previous terms.

Name: Contract
Documentation: **The current Contract** is handed over once the contract record is updated to reflect the latest signed state and is marked current. It carries the authoritative legal agreement: party identities, terms, pricing, service levels, duration, and any amendments or renewal status. Because this version reaches renewal drafting as the baseline, the renewal team works from the most recent terms and amendments. This prevents renewal work from drifting onto an obsolete contract and missing changes that were just agreed.

Name: Contract
Documentation: **The current Contract** is released after the record is updated to the latest signed state and marked current. It carries party identities, terms, pricing, service levels, duration, and any amendments or renewal status. Because this authoritative version reaches negotiation, each position is anchored in today's contract terms. This protects the negotiation from being driven by stale or superseded provisions, so the conversation reflects only what is currently agreed and avoids divergence from the latest agreement.

Name: Contract
Documentation: **The current Contract** moves forward after the record is updated to the latest signed state and marked current. It carries the authoritative agreement: party identities, terms, pricing, service levels, duration, and any amendments or renewal status. When the renewal is presented, this current version becomes the reference point, so the terms shown to the customer match the contract exactly as it stands. This prevents the presented renewal from contradicting the current contract state and keeps the proposal consistent with the latest agreement.

Name: Contract
Documentation: **The current Contract** is handed over once the record reflects the latest signed state and is marked current. It carries party identities, terms, pricing, service levels, duration, and any amendments or renewal status. Each incoming request is then checked against these active terms, confirming entitlement, scope, and pricing before any work proceeds. This protects request handling from proceeding without a valid contractual basis, so only requests that fit the current agreement move forward.

Name: Contract
Documentation: **The current Contract** is issued once the record is updated to the latest signed state and marked current. It carries party identities, terms, pricing, service levels, duration, and any amendments or renewal status. With this authoritative version in place, each new order is created using the contract's current pricing and only the items the agreement allows. This prevents order creation from lacking a valid contractual basis and ensures every order line reflects the latest agreed terms.

Name: Impact Assessment
Documentation: **Regulatory impact assessment enables applicability screening** once a regulatory announcement is analysed and its potential impact documented. It details the new or changed obligation, the affected activities, the expected compliance burden, and the preliminary relevance to current operations. This analysed basis allows the assessment to be screened against current operations to determine whether the obligation applies. The handover ensures obligations are examined rather than remaining unexamined, and the applicability review has a documented starting point.

Name: Applicability Determination
Documentation: **Applicability determination drives policy updates** when the impact assessment is evaluated and a clear applicability decision is reached. It records whether the obligation applies, which activities or locations are affected, and the reason for that determination. This binding input triggers creation or revision of compliance policies for the affected areas. The handover closes operational gaps by ensuring policies are updated for the new obligation rather than leaving them unchanged. Policy development receives a reliable scope for the affected areas.

Name: Compliance Policy
Documentation: **Network compliance mapping relies on policy.** A **Compliance Policy** states the required behaviour, control points, responsible roles, and compliance thresholds for an obligation. It is issued when the policy is approved and published, arriving as the authoritative statement of compliance requirements. Its arrival causes the policy to be mapped to the applicable suppliers, locations, and materials in the network, ensuring the network has assigned compliance obligations for this policy, covering every applicable supplier, location, and material.

Name: Compliance Policy
Documentation: **Monitoring and audit need defined requirements.** A **Compliance Policy** states the required behaviour, control points, responsible roles, and compliance thresholds for an obligation. It is issued when the policy is approved and published, arriving as the authoritative statement of compliance requirements. Its arrival causes monitoring checks and audit criteria to be derived from the policy, ensuring monitoring and audit activities have defined compliance requirements to test.

Name: Policy Mapping
Documentation: **Policy map defines monitoring scope** when all relevant network elements are associated with the policy. It connects each compliance policy to the specific network nodes, materials, and activities it governs, along with thresholds and evidence requirements. This complete coverage definition allows monitoring and audit to focus on the mapped elements and compare actual performance to policy thresholds. The handover ensures obligations are checked at the correct points rather than leaving monitoring without a defined scope.

Name: Regulatory Announcement
Documentation: **A Regulatory Announcement triggers impact assessment.** It carries the official text, effective date, issuing body, and any accompanying guidance for a new or changed obligation. Once captured from the monitoring source and recorded, it arrives as the original trigger for impact analysis. Its arrival means the regulatory content is analysed for operational impact and preliminary scope. This handover makes impact analysis possible and prevents the organisation from remaining unaware of the obligation.

Name: Audit Report
Documentation: **Audit Report communicates verified compliance findings.** It contains findings, evidence, nonconformities, and the compliance status of the audited network elements. Once monitoring and audit activities are complete and findings are verified, it arrives as the factual record of compliance performance. Its arrival causes compliance results to be communicated to oversight bodies and internal stakeholders. This handover ensures audit findings do not remain uncommunicated, and corrective actions can be initiated as a result.

Name: Request Assessment
Documentation: **Request Assessment enables proposal drafting.** It records the request scope, item specifications, quantities, required delivery or service dates, and any commercial constraints affecting proposal development. Issued after the request is reviewed and determined actionable with all mandatory fields completed, it arrives only when the request is clear enough for proposal drafting. Its arrival causes a proposal draft to be built using the assessed scope and constraints. This handover ensures proposal drafting has verified request details and a draft can be produced.

Name: Proposal Draft
Documentation: **Proposal Draft becomes formally initiated.** It contains the proposed scope, solution, pricing, timeline, and terms references assembled from the request assessment. Issued when the draft proposal is complete and internally reviewed, it arrives ready for formal initiation. Its arrival causes the proposal to be assigned a formal identifier and prepared for submission or negotiation. This handover ensures the proposal moves beyond working material and gains the official status needed for subsequent steps.

Name: Contract Proposal
Documentation: **Formal submission needs a complete package.** A **Contract Proposal** packages the final proposal terms, pricing, scope, and compliance references for formal submission to the requesting party. It is issued when the proposal is initiated and approved for external submission, arriving as the submission-ready version. Its arrival causes the proposal to be delivered to the requesting party with a formal submission record, ensuring the requesting party receives an offer to consider.

Name: Contract Proposal
Documentation: **Negotiation needs a formal starting point.** A **Contract Proposal** packages the final proposal terms, pricing, scope, and compliance references for formal submission or negotiation. It is issued when the proposal is initiated and enters the negotiation path, arriving as a negotiation version. Its arrival causes the proposal to be refined and negotiated between parties, giving the negotiation a formal proposal to work from and ensuring the discussions are structured around that formal proposal.

Name: Proposal Submission Record
Documentation: **Proposal Submission Record confirms formal submission.** It captures the date, recipient, delivery channel, and version of the proposal submitted. Issued when the proposal is submitted and receipt is logged, it arrives as evidence of the formal submission. Its arrival allows negotiation to proceed on the basis of the submitted version. This handover prevents ambiguity about whether a proposal was submitted and gives negotiation a fixed reference point for the discussions.

Name: Revised Proposal
Documentation: **Revised Proposal carries agreed negotiation outcomes.** It includes the updated terms, concessions, and scope adjustments agreed during negotiation. Issued when negotiation produces a revised version that all parties accept as final, it arrives ready for formal approval. Its arrival causes the revised terms to be routed for internal approvals. This handover ensures approvals are sought against the current agreed terms and the agreed changes are formally endorsed as part of the approval process.

Name: Approval Packet
Documentation: **Approval Packet enables signature collection.** This packet bundles the proposal, the approval records, approver names, approval dates, and any conditions attached to each approval. It is issued once all required approvals are obtained and the packet is complete. At that point the packet serves as the authorised basis for signature, and signature collection begins on the approved proposal. Without this packet, no signing takes place and the approved terms remain unsigned.

Name: Approval Packet
Documentation: **Approval Packet triggers contract release preparation.** This packet bundles the proposal, the approval records, approver names, approval dates, and any conditions attached to each approval. It is issued once all required approvals are obtained and the packet is complete. At that point the packet serves as the authorised basis for contract release, and release preparation begins using the approved terms. Without this packet, release work has no approval evidence and the contract is not issued.

Name: Signed Contract
Documentation: **Signed Contract releases the executed agreement.** It carries the fully executed agreement with all signatures, dates, and the final negotiated terms. Issued when all parties sign and the signature authority is verified, it arrives as a legally binding contract. Its arrival causes the contract to be released and activated. This handover ensures the agreement does not remain unexecuted and makes the contract available for use as a binding agreement.

Name: Contract
Documentation: **The released contract** carries the current legal agreement: party identities, terms, pricing, service levels, duration, and any amendments or renewal status. It is issued when the contract is released and active, arriving as the authoritative version governing the relationship. Renewal drafting then uses this released contract as its baseline, ensuring that new terms are built from the active agreement. This authoritative version prevents renewal work from starting without the current contract terms.

Name: Contract
Documentation: **The released contract** carries the current legal agreement: party identities, terms, pricing, service levels, duration, and any amendments or renewal status. It is issued when the contract is released and active, arriving as the authoritative version governing the relationship. Negotiation then anchors its positions in this released contract, keeping discussions aligned to the current terms. This authoritative version protects negotiation from ever being based on an obsolete or non-released agreement.

Name: Contract
Documentation: **The released contract** carries the current legal agreement: party identities, terms, pricing, service levels, duration, and any amendments or renewal status. It is issued when the contract is released and active, arriving as the authoritative version governing the relationship. When renewal terms are presented, this released contract serves as the reference, grounding the proposal in the current agreement. This authoritative reference ensures that presented renewal terms do not lack a contractual basis.

Name: Contract
Documentation: **The released contract** carries the current legal agreement: party identities, terms, pricing, service levels, duration, and any amendments or renewal status. It is issued when the contract is released and active, arriving as the authoritative version governing the relationship. Incoming requests are validated against this released contract, so that entitlement, scope, and pricing are confirmed before handling proceeds. This authoritative check prevents requests from being handled without confirmation of what the contract covers.

Name: Contract
Documentation: **The released contract** carries approved terms, pricing schedules, service levels, delivery locations, change-control clauses, version number, effective date, renewal terms, and signatory identifiers. It is issued only after legal review, budget approval, and dual-party sign-off are complete, and its arrival means the agreement is in force and available for amendment. Amendment and renewal then proceed under the change-control terms in this contract. This contract provides the contractual anchor needed for binding amendments, so proposed changes do not lack a reference point.

Name: Contract
Documentation: **The released contract** carries the commercial terms that authorise purchase orders: item pricing, quantity breaks, lead times, delivery locations, supplier identification, validity dates, and maximum commitment values. It is issued only after award approval and signature, meaning the buying entity holds a usable agreement against which orders are placed. Purchase orders for the covered items are then created, each referencing this agreement and inheriting its pricing and terms. This contract is what enables those orders to be placed without renegotiating terms for each request.

Name: Sustainability Goal Analysis
Documentation: **Sustainability Goal Analysis sets priority ranking.** The analysis records each sustainability goal, its current performance baseline, the gap to target, and the affected operational areas. It includes numeric indicators, baseline dates, and ownership assignments. It is produced when goal data has been collected and compared against targets, and its arrival means the gap picture is complete enough to set priorities. Decision makers use the analysis to order gaps by impact and urgency. Without this analysis, priorities are assigned without the quantified gap picture, and effort is directed by assumption rather than measurement.

Name: Sustainability Goal Analysis
Documentation: **Sustainability Goal Analysis starts gap treatment.** It carries the same goal baseline, gap values, and affected operational areas as the version used for priority setting. It also lists the specific gaps requiring treatment and the indicators used to detect them. It is produced when goals are compared with current performance and gaps are quantified, meaning treatment begins with measured gaps rather than anecdote. Upon arrival, each documented gap is assigned to a treatment owner and a target closure date. Without this analysis, gap treatment starts without measured baselines, and remediation addresses unverified symptoms.

Name: Supply Chain Priority List
Documentation: **Supply Chain Priority List ranks goals.** It orders the sustainability goals by business impact, regulatory exposure, and resource requirement. Each entry includes a rank, the underlying sustainability goal, the affected supply chain area, and the rationale for its position. Issued when priorities are agreed and signed off, its arrival means gap identification starts from an endorsed sequence, not an unordered goal set. Its arrival directs gap identification to examine the highest-ranked goals first and records gaps against that priority order. This handover prevents gap identification from treating all goals as equally urgent and ensures resources are focused according to ranking.

Name: Sustainability Gap Register
Documentation: **Sustainability Gap Register sets monitoring baseline.** The register lists each gap between current sustainability performance and the stated goal. It records the gap description, affected area, current and target values, measurement method, and the date each gap was identified. It is issued when goals have been compared with current performance and discrepancies are documented, meaning the full set of known gaps is centralised and ready for monitoring. Evaluators use the register to track closure progress against the recorded current and target values. Without this register, no central record of sustainability gaps exists, and monitoring relies on scattered point-in-time observations.

Name: Sustainability Gap Register
Documentation: **Sustainability Gap Register selects treatment candidates.** It carries the same gap entries, target values, and affected areas as the monitoring copy, and also records the severity classification and the date each gap was accepted for treatment. It is issued when gap identification is complete and each gap is assigned a severity rating, meaning treatment teams have the authoritative list of gaps to address. Upon arrival, each entry in the register becomes a treatment candidate with its target value and deadline. Without this register, treatment teams operate without a confirmed gap backlog, and gaps are addressed only when reported informally.

Name: Sustainability Performance Assessment
Documentation: **Sustainability Performance Assessment is ready** once monitoring data for the reporting period is collected and validated. The Sustainability Performance Assessment summarises measured progress against each sustainability goal: current values, trend direction, variance from target, and status of previously treated gaps. Its arrival means the period's sustainability results are ready for external and internal communication. Reporting of results then takes place; stakeholders receive the assessment with the period's achievements and shortfalls. This handover ensures stakeholders have the period-end score and the measured progress statement.

Name: Sustainability Action Plan
Documentation: **Sustainability Action Plan is issued** when gap treatment actions are selected and approved. The Sustainability Action Plan specifies the correction actions for each gap: action owner, due date, required resources, and the target value each action is expected to achieve. Its arrival means planned corrective work is committed and ready for tracking. Progress monitoring against the plan begins; each action's completion status and achieved value are tracked against its due date. This handover ensures monitoring has a committed action set and gap closures are verified.

Name: Analysis Finding
Documentation: **Analysis Finding is produced** when a distributed report is reviewed and a deviation is detected. The Analysis Finding states an observed performance deviation, the performance report it came from, the affected process area, and the magnitude of the variance. Its arrival means the deviation is documented and ready for causal investigation. The causal investigation is triggered; the finding is decomposed into contributing events and conditions by the root-cause workflow. This handover ensures performance deviations receive root-cause analysis rather than remaining unexplained.

Name: Root Cause Record
Documentation: **Root Cause Record is produced** when causal analysis reaches a verified cause with supporting evidence. The Root Cause Record names a confirmed cause of a performance deviation, the evidence linking it to the effect, and the conditions under which it occurs. Its arrival means the cause is ready for priority ranking against other causes. The cause is added to the ranking set, and each record is scored for impact and frequency. This handover ensures prioritisation operates on verified cause entries rather than hypotheses.

Name: Corrective Action Plan
Documentation: **Corrective Action Plan is issued** when solution options are evaluated and one is chosen for each priority root cause. The Corrective Action Plan contains the selected countermeasures, including implementation steps, owners, due dates, and success criteria. Its arrival means the corrective work is approved and scheduled. The improvement monitoring cycle starts; implementing teams execute the actions and report completion against due dates. This handover ensures each identified root cause has an approved correction path and performance gaps begin to close.

Name: Improvement Progress Report
Documentation: **Improvement Progress Report is produced** when the improvement program is reviewed at the end of a monitoring interval. The Improvement Progress Report records the status of each corrective action—started, on hold, completed, or overdue—along with completion percentages, milestone dates, and revised forecasts. Its arrival gives stakeholders a current view of action progress. The report is distributed and used to raise attention on overdue or blocked actions. This handover ensures overdue corrective actions are noticed rather than overlooked.

Name: Prioritized Root Cause List
Documentation: **Prioritized Root Cause List directs solution development.** The list ranks confirmed root causes by impact, occurrence frequency, and ease of correction. Each entry references the original Root Cause Record and includes the priority score. It is issued when all root cause records from the analysis period are scored and ordered, meaning the highest-priority causes are handed over for solution design. Designers allocate effort according to the list's order, starting with the highest-ranked causes. Without this list, solution work starts without an agreed cause priority, and low-impact causes consume resources ahead of high-impact ones.

Name: Prioritized Root Cause List
Documentation: **Prioritized Root Cause List communicates ranked causes.** This list is the same ranked set used for solution design. It carries the priority order, scores, and referenced Root Cause Records for communication to stakeholders. It is issued when the priority scoring is approved, meaning the ranked causes are ready for reporting to owners and leadership. Upon arrival, the list is distributed so stakeholders see the ordering and the criteria behind each score. Without this list, the reporting cycle has no priority result to communicate, and decision makers lack the ranked view.

Name: Performance Report
Documentation: **Performance Report triggers deviation analysis.** The report presents measurement results for a defined reporting period: actual values, plan values, variances, and trend indicators for the processes covered, along with metadata about the reporting period and validation status. It is issued after the report is run, checked, and approved for distribution; its arrival means the period's results are ready for analytical review. This handover enables analysts to scan variances and trends to identify deviations. It protects against performance outcomes remaining unanalysed and deviations going undetected from the period's data.

Name: Performance Report
Documentation: **Performance Report carries plan variance** — the same actual-versus-plan values and cumulative variance used for general analysis, but directed at supply chain plan deviations specifically, including plan reference and actual output. It is issued after validation and distribution, and its arrival means the variance data is available for deviation analysis. Planners compare actuals to the plan and classify each variance by cause. Only after this report arrives can supply chain plan deviations be identified and the plan adjusted to reflect realised conditions.

Name: Performance Report
Documentation: **Performance Report enables forecast validation** — it carries actual demand observations, the previously forecast values for the same period, and forecast error per item or category across the demand horizon under review. Its arrival after the reporting period closes means the demand forecast is compared against realised demand. Forecast error is then computed and the forecast model is adjusted where the error exceeds tolerance. This handover is what ensures demand forecast accuracy is checked and the next forecast cycle uses validated assumptions instead of unvalidated ones.

Name: Performance Report
Documentation: **Performance Report delivers delivery variances** — promised delivery dates, actual delivery dates, and variance per shipment or delivery area, plus carrier performance indicators when collected. Produced when delivery events are recorded and the reporting period ends, its arrival means delivery plan deviation data is ready for analysis. Late and early deliveries are then flagged and their impact on the delivery plan is assessed. This handover is what makes it possible to analyse delivery plan deviations and correct repeated lateness at the plan level.

Name: Risk Analysis Record
Documentation: **Risk Analysis Record captures** the assessed likelihood and impact of a risk, the analysis method used, and supporting assumptions or data sources. It is produced when a risk from the register has been analysed and its characteristics are understood, signalling that the risk is ready for evaluation. Evaluation compares the assessed likelihood and impact to acceptance thresholds, moving the risk toward an acceptability decision. The handover ensures no risk remains unevaluated; with the record in hand, each analysed risk is judged against formal criteria.

Name: Risk Register
Documentation: **Risk Register carries** the full set of identified risks, including current status, analysis results, risk owners, and review dates. It is updated each time a risk is analysed, and is issued after those updates, giving the monitoring cycle the current risk state. Monitoring then reviews every risk entry against its trigger conditions and warning indicators. With the register in hand, the monitoring cycle operates on the latest likelihood and impact values, so emerging changes in risk status are detected rather than missed.

Name: Risk Register
Documentation: **Risk Register serves** as the reference record for external risk reporting, carrying risk entries, analysis results, and owner assignments. It is issued after the risk analysis updates are approved, which means the current risk set is ready for communication. Reporting uses this register to send stakeholders the latest analysed likelihood and impact values. The handover ensures that risk reports are built from approved, current analysis, so stakeholders see accurate risk levels rather than stale ones.

Name: Risk Criteria
Documentation: **Risk Criteria set the assessment standard.** They define the organisation's risk appetite: likelihood and impact scales, threshold levels for acceptance, and rules for prioritising risks. They are issued when context and risk appetite are agreed, so risk analysis follows a consistent measurement scale. With them, analysts apply the defined scales and thresholds to each risk, making likelihood and impact ratings comparable across all risks. This handover protects against ad hoc scales that would leave ratings incomparable.

Name: Risk Criteria
Documentation: **Risk Criteria carry evaluation thresholds.** They carry the same acceptance thresholds and impact-likelihood scales used in analysis, plus the risk evaluation decision rules. They are issued when the risk appetite is set, so evaluation compares risks against a fixed set of criteria. On arrival, analysed risks are compared to the acceptance thresholds; risks above threshold are marked for treatment, those below are accepted. This handover provides fixed reference thresholds, preventing inconsistent acceptance decisions.

Name: Context Statement
Documentation: **Context Statement sets the risk boundaries.** It describes the organisational environment, scope of risk management, stakeholder concerns, and the external and internal factors that influence risk. It is produced when the risk management context is defined and approved, so risk identification starts from a common understanding of what is in scope. On arrival, risk identification is directed to the areas and events described in the statement; identifiers look for risks within the defined boundaries. This handover protects against risks outside the stated boundary never being considered.

Name: Risk Evaluation Decision
Documentation: **Each evaluated risk gets a disposition.** The **Risk Evaluation Decision** records the outcome for every risk: accepted, treated, transferred, or avoided, together with the rationale and the threshold value applied. This record is produced once the risk is compared against the risk criteria and a decision is made. It makes the evaluated outcome available for reporting; stakeholders see which risks are accepted and which require treatment, and risk owners are informed of required actions.

Name: Prioritized Risk Register
Documentation: **Risk treatment gets its queue.** The **Prioritized Risk Register** lists risks in order of treatment urgency, combining the evaluation decision, risk level, and treatment owner. Each entry includes the selected risk response. This register is issued when evaluated risks are ranked and treatment owners are assigned. It makes the treatment workflow actionable: owners develop responses for the highest-ranked risks first, ensuring high-risk items are not left waiting behind lower-ranked ones.

Name: Risk Register
Documentation: **Risk Register is issued** when risk identification is complete and each risk is documented with an owner. The Risk Register contains each identified risk with its description, risk category, potential causes, and initial owner. Its arrival means the identified risk set is ready for analysis. Analysis of each entry is triggered; each risk is examined for likelihood and impact. This handover ensures risk analysis has an identified risk set to assess.

Name: Risk Monitoring Report
Documentation: **Risk Monitoring Report is produced** when the risk monitoring cycle completes a review interval. The Risk Monitoring Report records changes in risk status since the last review: new risks, closed risks, risk level changes, and trigger events that have occurred, along with trend information and review dates. Its arrival means the current risk state is ready for communication. Distribution of monitoring findings follows; stakeholders see which risks have increased, decreased, or materialised. This handover ensures risk owners are informed of changes in their assigned risks.

Name: Purchase Order
Documentation: **The Purchase Order** arrives when an approved need is matched to a supplier and contract terms, carrying line items, quantities, agreed prices, requested delivery date, supplier details, and the contract reference. This handover lets inspection planning use those line items to prepare criteria and compare incoming goods against the ordered specifications. As a result, any nonconformity is referenced to the purchase order, so inspection never relies on ad hoc standards or misses a mismatch to what was actually agreed.

Name: Purchase Order
Documentation: **The Purchase Order** is issued once the order is approved and transmitted, carrying line items, quantities, supplier details, delivery instructions, and acceptance terms. Its arrival signals that specific goods are expected and gives the receiving area the exact reference needed to validate incoming shipments against ordered items and quantities. This prevents acceptance from falling back on ad hoc criteria, so every delivery is matched to the purchase order before it is accepted.

Name: Purchase Order
Documentation: **The Purchase Order** is issued when the order is approved and the supplier has accepted it. It carries the commercial commitment: item prices, payment terms, billing address, and the supplier's banking details if held, authorising supplier invoicing up to the order value. This handover triggers payment matching, so each supplier invoice is compared to the order's prices and quantities before payment is approved. That comparison prevents price or quantity discrepancies from going unnoticed and ensures invoices are paid only when they match the commercial commitment.

Name: Purchase Order
Documentation: **Purchase order carries staging details** The purchase order includes item identifiers, quantities, storage location requirements, and staging instructions needed to prepare received goods for subsequent use. When an order includes staging requirements, its arrival signals the staging area what is coming and how to allocate space. The receiving and staging area reserves space and resources in advance, ensuring incoming goods are placed according to plan instead of decided on the spot.

Name: Purchase Order
Documentation: **Purchase order enables receiving matching** The purchase order carries ordered line items, quantities, supplier identification, and expected delivery date, and is the same order record used for inspection and payment matching. Issued when the order is approved and sent to the supplier, its arrival gives the receiving location an order to match against incoming deliveries. The receiving workflow checks each incoming delivery against the order's line items and quantities, logging discrepancies and giving every acceptance decision a contractual baseline.

Name: Supplier Shortlist
Documentation: **A vetted supplier shortlist** contains each candidate's name, capabilities, past performance and initial commercial terms, after market screening and prequalification. With this list, negotiation and award can begin: only shortlisted suppliers are invited to submit binding offers, and award decisions rest on a vetted candidate set. This handover protects the process from being conducted with unqualified suppliers, so the final choice is built on screened options. It makes the negotiation phase meaningful because every invited supplier has already met the sourcing criteria.

Name: Goods Acceptance
Documentation: **Goods Acceptance after inspection** records the result: accepted and rejected items, quantities, condition notes, and the inspector's signature. It is issued once inspection is complete and goods meet acceptance criteria, authorising accepted goods for storage. With this record, accepted quantities can be moved to assigned storage locations and inventory records are updated. This handover ensures inspected goods do not remain in limbo and inventory is updated for every accepted item.

Name: Award Decision
Documentation: **Award Decision to create orders** identifies the selected supplier, awarded price and terms, contract reference, and any award conditions. It is produced when negotiation concludes and a supplier is chosen, giving purchasing an approved source to order against. With this decision, purchase orders for the awarded scope are created and inherit the agreed terms. The handover makes the purchase intent executable, so the awarded goods or services are ordered only after a vetted decision is in place.

Name: Inventory Record
Documentation: **Inventory Record after put-away** states the storage location, item identifier, quantity on hand, batch or lot, and put-away date. It is issued when the physical count is confirmed, giving the picking operation accurate location and quantity information. This record enables pickers to locate items and reserve the available quantity for outbound requests. The handover keeps picking from working with stale or missing stock positions, so requested items are found at their recorded location.

Name: Goods Receipt
Documentation: **A delivery is received.** The **Goods Receipt** records that a delivery has arrived: supplier, purchase order reference, item count, condition at arrival, and the receiving timestamp. It is issued when the carrier's delivery is unloaded and the shipment is matched to an order. This record signals that the goods are ready for inspection. Inspectors use the receipt to confirm identities and quantities before quality checks, so received goods are inspected and nonconforming items are detected before storage.

Name: Goods Receipt
Documentation: **Proof of delivery enables payment.** The **Goods Receipt** carries the confirmed received quantities, supplier identifier, purchase order reference, and the date goods were taken into custody. It is the proof-of-delivery record used in three-way matching. This record is issued when the shipment is received and counted. It gives the payment approval process evidence that goods arrived as ordered. The receipt is compared to the purchase order and supplier invoice, and payment is approved only when all three agree, so payment decisions verify delivery.

Name: Return Authorization
Documentation: **Return Authorization carries approved terms** — the return reason, item identifiers, quantity, condition, and disposition instruction, with the originating transaction and customer identity. It is issued only after the return request is validated against the return policy and the original transaction, and its arrival means the return is approved and authorised to proceed. The authorization provides the customer with return terms and initiates the return movement. Only with this authorization can goods movement or credit activity be permitted and the return inquiry closed.

Name: Return Authorization
Documentation: **Return Authorization authorises physical acceptance** — it carries the approved return reason, item identifiers, expected quantity, condition requirements, and the disposition route for the returned items. Issued only when the return request passes policy validation, its arrival at the receiving point means the return is authorised for physical acceptance. Returned items are then accepted against the authorized quantity and condition. Only with this authorization are inbound units accepted rather than refused or held, and a return receipt recorded.

Name: Return Authorization
Documentation: **Return Authorization clears inspection** — it specifies the item identifiers, return quantity, reported defect, and the inspection criteria that apply to the returned goods. Issued after the return is validated, its arrival means the returned item is cleared for inspection under the stated criteria. The inspection step then has the approved basis to evaluate the return against the authorized quantity and condition. Only with this authorization does inspection have an approved reference for the return, allowing the item to be processed rather than held.

Name: Return Authorization
Documentation: **Return Authorization carries financial terms** — approved refund or replacement terms, item condition expectations, and the financial value to be credited. It is issued only after return policy validation and original transaction matching, and its arrival means the return is authorised for financial settlement. The settlement calculation then applies the authorized return terms to the returned item and issues the credit or replacement. This authorization is what allows the return to be settled financially, issuing the credit or replacement and closing the return financially.

Name: Solution Proposal
Documentation: **Solution Proposal for customer presentation** contains the proposed configuration, scope, price, delivery date, assumptions, and customer-specific requirements addressed by the design. It is issued after the solution has been developed against refreshed customer needs, signalling that the proposal is ready to present. With this proposal, the customer can evaluate the offer against their needs. This handover ensures the opportunity advances to feedback and negotiation because a concrete solution is presented rather than left undeveloped.

Name: Renewal Request
Documentation: **Renewal Request with customer consent** carries the contract identifier, expiry date, current terms, consumption volumes, and the customer's consent to renew. It is issued when the renewal window opens and the customer has expressed intent to continue, authorising renewal work. With this request, the renewal is scheduled for negotiation and fulfilment planning. This handover ensures the contract does not approach expiry without scheduled action, and service or supply continuation is planned rather than left unplanned.

Name: Inspection Report
Documentation: **Inspection clears items for storage.** The **Inspection Report** records the item identifier, quantity inspected, quantity accepted, quantity rejected, condition notes, and the storage or disposition instruction. It is issued after physical inspection is complete and the inspector has recorded findings against the expected condition. The report authorises accepted items to be placed into their designated storage locations and inventory availability to be updated. This ensures accepted items move out of inspection hold and into storage.

Name: Inspection Report
Documentation: **Return inspection finalises settlement.** The **Inspection Report** records the returned item condition, accepted quantity, rejected quantity, and the financial disposition relevant to the return. It is issued after inspection findings are finalised, providing the return settlement with the factual basis for credit or replacement. The settlement amount is then calculated from the accepted quantity and condition recorded, so the return does not remain open and a credit or replacement is issued.

Name: Presentation Record
Documentation: **Presentation Record of customer feedback** documents the solution presented, the customer's questions, objections, and any feedback captured during the presentation session. It is issued after the solution is presented, formally recording the customer's reactions. This record allows the feedback to be reviewed and incorporated into the next iteration of the solution. The handover protects subsequent solution development from proceeding on outdated assumptions by keeping the captured customer feedback available for reference.

Name: Inventory Record
Documentation: **Inventory Availability after putaway** states the item identifier, quantity on hand, storage location, and status of each stock unit after putaway. It is issued when the physical putaway is confirmed and the system location matches the physical location, meaning stock is available to promise. With this availability record, the picking step receives the location and quantity to retrieve for open orders. This handover ensures picking operates with confirmed stock and issues retrieval instructions, rather than working without confirmed stock.

Name: Receiving Record
Documentation: **Received goods are recorded.** The **Receiving Record** carries the supplier, purchase order reference, received quantity, condition at receipt, and the carrier details. It is issued when the inbound shipment is unloaded and matched against the purchase order. This record marks the goods as physically received and initiates their transfer from the receiving area to a storage or staging location. The transfer is initiated as soon as the record is issued. It ensures the goods are processed and onward movement is planned.

Name: Updated Customer Needs
Documentation: **Customer Needs Update keeps solution design** current by recording changes in the customer’s requirements, priorities, timeline, and constraints since the last engagement. It is produced after the customer situation is refreshed and the updated needs are confirmed. That arrival means the development effort works from the latest requirement baseline. The solution is then built against the updated needs, replacing outdated assumptions. This protects the solution from reflecting stale requirements and ensures it addresses the customer’s current situation instead of missing it.

Name: Sales Order
Documentation: **Sales Order commits demand** with customer, item identifiers, quantities, pricing, requested delivery date, and ship-to details. It is issued only after the order is validated for completeness and price, and its arrival means the demand is committed and available for fulfilment planning. This committed demand allows the fulfilment schedule to be created against the ordered items and dates. That handover is what prevents the demand from remaining unplanned and ensures the schedule reflects the full order.

Name: Sales Order
Documentation: **Sales Order carries payment obligation** with customer, billing details, payment terms, and the total value of the ordered items. It is issued after the order passes initial validation, and its arrival means the financial obligation is ready for assessment. That readiness allows the payment approval to evaluate the customer's credit position and the order value, completing the financial assessment. This handover ensures the order can proceed to fulfilment for those ordered items.

Name: Capacity Exception
Documentation: **Capacity Exception flags schedule overload** by identifying the schedule line, resource, period, required load, and available capacity along with the resulting shortage. It is issued when a proposed schedule exceeds available capacity for a resource, signalling that the schedule is infeasible as planned. When this arrives, make order scheduling rebalances the load or moves work to an alternate period. That keeps the overload from remaining undetected and protects the schedule from committing to capacity that is not actually available.

Name: Inspection Report
Documentation: **Inspection Report authorises stock transfer** with item identifier, inspection result, accepted quantity, and the storage condition required for accepted units. It is issued when inspection completes and the units are determined fit for stock, so its arrival authorises the transfer of accepted goods to inventory. That authorisation is what moves accepted units to their storage locations and updates the inventory position to reflect the new stock. This handover keeps accepted units from remaining in the inspection area with no inventory record.

Name: Nonconformity Report
Documentation: **Nonconformity Report triggers disposal** with item, failed inspection criterion, quantity affected, and the disposition instruction for nonconforming units. It is issued when inspection finds units that do not meet the expected condition, and its arrival means the nonconforming material is formally identified for disposal. That formal identification allows the nonconforming units to be disposed of according to the report and the inventory to be adjusted. This handover prevents nonconforming units from remaining in inventory and contaminating stock records.

Name: Goods Receipt
Documentation: **Goods Receipt confirms accepted stock** by recording the purchase order reference, supplier, received quantity, and item condition upon receipt. It is issued when the physical receipt is completed and matched to the purchase order, meaning the goods are accepted into the organisation’s custody. The received goods are then put away into storage or staging locations. This keeps the goods moving out of the receiving area and ensures the putaway instruction is issued.

Name: Inventory Availability
Documentation: **Inventory Availability prevents overcommitment** by stating the item identifier, quantity on hand, location, and status of stock after putaway. It is issued when the putaway is confirmed and inventory records match the physical stock, giving the schedule the latest available quantity to promise. The schedule is then created using the confirmed available quantity, avoiding overcommitment. This protects the schedule from being built on stale stock and prevents commitments to inventory that is not actually available.

Name: Inventory Availability
Documentation: **Inventory Availability captures transferred stock** by stating the item identifier, quantity on hand, location, and status of stock after a transfer between locations. It is issued when the transfer is completed and the inventory records reflect the movement, giving the schedule the updated stock position. The schedule is then created with the transferred quantity available for promising. This prevents the schedule from excluding the transferred stock and ensures the available quantity is not understated.

Name: Unloading Record
Documentation: **Unloading Record validates what arrived** by carrying the carrier, delivery reference, number of units unloaded, and any damage or discrepancy noted at the dock. It is issued when the inbound shipment is physically unloaded, meaning the goods are on the receiving dock and ready for receipt verification. The receiving step then verifies the unloaded units against the purchase order and records any discrepancy. This gives the receipt a basis to confirm what arrived and validates the shipment, preventing an unverified receipt.

Name: Network Constraint Register
Documentation: **Network Constraint Register guides solution design** by listing each constraint found across the network, including location, capacity, lead time, and service limitation, with its impact. It is issued after all network constraints are analysed and recorded, so its arrival means solution definition has the full set of restricting factors. That full set allows network solutions to be defined within the recorded constraints, avoiding proposals that violate them. This handover prevents solutions from being designed against incomplete constraints and failing during execution.

Name: Network Constraint Register
Documentation: **Network Constraint Register priorities roadmap changes** by enumerating the binding constraints on the network, each with its location, magnitude, and operational impact. It is issued when constraint analysis is complete, and its arrival means the change roadmap has the validated list of restrictions that must be resolved. That validated list allows the roadmap to sequence changes to address the most binding constraints first. This handover prevents the roadmap from prioritising changes without evidence and targeting constraints that are not confirmed.

Name: Network Performance Report
Documentation: **Network Performance Report grounds organisational analysis** by capturing throughput, delivery performance, cost per unit, asset utilisation, and service failures across the network. It is issued after performance data is collected and analysed for the network, so its arrival means organisational analysis has a factual baseline. That factual baseline allows the organisational analysis to correlate performance shortfalls with roles and structure. This handover prevents the analysis from proceeding without measured outcomes and identifying no verified performance gaps.

Name: Network Performance Report
Documentation: **Network Performance Report focuses metric attention** by presenting measured performance levels, variances from target, and the metrics that show the largest gaps. It is issued when network performance has been analysed against targets, so its arrival means metric prioritisation has the measured evidence required. That evidence allows the metrics with the largest performance gaps to be prioritised for management attention. This handover prevents metric prioritisation from relying on opinion and missing the gaps that actually constrain the network.

Name: Tax Impact Assessment
Documentation: **Tax Impact Assessment guides network decisions** by computing the tax obligations, incentives, and exemptions associated with each candidate network configuration. It is produced after the supply chain strategy is analysed for tax implications, giving the network definition the tax position of each option. The supply chain network is then defined with the tax impact accounted for, selecting configurations that minimise exposure. This protects the network from being defined without the tax cost and prevents unplanned liabilities later.

Name: Assignment Record
Documentation: **Assignment Record authorises implementation** by naming the owner, the action to be implemented, the due date, and the scope of work. It is issued when an action has been determined and assigned to a responsible party, meaning implementation is authorised to begin.
